- Experience operating LLM systems with observability and quality monitoring in production.

- GIS familiarity (parcels, zoning layers, geocoding).

- Multi-country product experience (heterogeneous sources, localization, varying rules).

- NLP background

Why Join Us 

You're joining a team of 9 at the very beginning - where every decision you make shapes the product, the culture, and the trajectory of the company. What you build here will be yours.

- Direct impact on growth: your work doesn't sit behind three layers of review. You ship, clients use it, and you see the results. Every output you improve translates directly into revenue and reputation.

- Real-world impact : your work supports investment decisions, accelerates development timelines, and helps redefine how cities are imagined, designed, and built.

- High ownership : own the full feasibility stack end to end, as the CEO of that part.

- Competitive salary and meaningful equity in an early-stage company.

- A small team with high standards - we ship fast and love working together.

More information about Davis, the team and the market we’re going after: 

Team 

Mehdi (Co-founder & CEO) grew up in a family of architects and has lived this problem firsthand. He's a repeat founder who bootstrapped his first startup at 20 , and graduated from Sciences Po and HEC Paris. Amine (Co-founder & CTO) is an AI researcher from École Polytechnique who worked extensively on discrete diffusion and turned down a PhD with Google DeepMind to build Davis . They started working together in July 2025 at Entrepreneur First's first European residency, a two-month lock-in in a German castle.

Today we're a team of 12 : technical profiles from Polytechnique, ENS and INRIA alongside architects and deep real estate expertise.

We're small with an extremely high bar . If you want to work deeply on hard problems and see your work reach clients within days, you're the one we need.

Why We'll Win 

Real estate is a $13 trillion industry that technology has largely bypassed. The professional services that feed it (design, engineering, feasibility, permitting) represent hundreds of billions in spend that no one has seriously automated.

Proptech spent the last decade selling SaaS on the edges of these workflows. It didn't work, for two reasons: no professional wants another tool to learn, and no tool can automate work that runs on expert judgment. Davis makes a different bet. We don't sell tools, we sell the work: AI-generated, expert-validated, delivered in days instead of weeks. Every project compounds our data advantage across typologies, geographies and regulatory contexts.

Why No One Has Solved Architectural Design Yet 

Real estate development bleeds time and money in architectural design loops. Architects cycle through dozens of floorplan revisions to meet regulatory and client constraints, each round taking days, each missed constraint restarting the loop. Traditional CAD and BIM tools offer zero generative capability ; parametric tools only check constraints after generation , leading to designs that frequently break under new zoning rules or irregular sites.

Generative AI has the potential to solve this , but doesn't yet. Fine-tuning image diffusion models on floorplans produces layouts that look plausible but fall apart under scrutiny: hallucinated rooms, mislabeled spaces, code violations no architect would accept. Pixel-space models have no concept of what a wall is or why a corridor needs to connect two things. Compliance-guidance techniques typically require segmentation at each noisy timestep, compounding errors and making major edits impractical. As a result, floorplans may “look” plausible but break building codes, or need heavy post-processing before they're usable.

description:

We're a team based in Paris, Detroit and Japan, and we're growing fast. Here's the role:

- Solid understanding of French GAAP, financial statements and month-end mechanics

- Fluent in French and English: both required, as you'll work with our US and Japanese teams

title: Change and Transformation Manager - Client Delivery (Fluency in French & English required)
description:
Change and Transformation Manager – Client Delivery (French/english) 

Location: Paris, France (hybrid, three days a week in the office; occasional travel to Brussels and London)
Level: Programme Manager senior 
Team: Client Delivery
Contract: Permanent
Reporting To: Operating Model Design Lead

Please note: This role is based in France, so you need to live here or be open to relocating, and it requires an existing right to work in the EU. We can’t offer visa sponsorship, but we review sponsorship role by role, so keep an eye on our careers site for future opportunities. 

Fluent French and English (spoken and written) are essential, and we kindly ask you to submit your CV in English. 

About Kaluza 

Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.

Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.

With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.

What you’ll do 

- Own change and transformation support for go-live readiness for ENGIE France’s migration onto Kaluza as the hands-on lead, from planning through cutover, hypercare and transition towards scaling, so ENGIE’s teams are ready and confident to adopt the platform from day one.

- Decide the change approach for the programme: stakeholder analysis, change impact assessment, training design and business readiness engagement, shaped to ENGIE France’s operating context and owned by their teams.

- Operate Kaluza’s business readiness governance: stage gates, readiness evidence, risk and dependency tracking and weekly reporting.

- Partner with the Learning and Adoption Specialist in France to coordinate training, Train the Trainer and knowledge content, so enablement lands throughout each programme increment as we build out and release features via Agile delivery.

- Be the day-to-day point of contact for ENGIE France on business readiness, change and adoption, giving practical change advice to their transformation leads.

- Track adoption and operational stability through hypercare, root-cause any shortfall against acceptance criteria, and agree interventions with ENGIE.

- Improve Kaluza’s readiness playbook: evolve what worked on ENGIE Belgium, test fixes where it falls short in France, and share what you learn with colleagues across Client Delivery to shape the platform’s operational foundations and improvements and to set our global standards.

Day to day, the activities you’ll lead or support include:

- Change impact and readiness planning: diagnosing the full scope of impacts across roles, workflows, systems and customer experience, then turning them into a prioritised readiness plan sequenced against delivery, migration and release cadence.

- Stakeholders, sponsors and change networks: mapping stakeholders and influence at workstream level, helping sponsors stay visible and engaged, and shaping the champion, superuser and people-manager networks that carry change into ENGIE’s business.

- Communications and resistance: supporting ENGIE France’s own communications and engagement strategy, so their teams and customers hear a consistent, positive story about the programme. You’ll help leaders and champions advocate for the change, internally and with customers, and anticipate where resistance may form so you can intervene before it becomes entrenched.

- Migration and go-live readiness: building the business and operational readiness evidence that enables a smooth transfer to service, measured against the agreed acceptance criteria, and supporting the go-live command centre.

- Hypercare and stabilisation: agreeing hypercare entry and exit criteria, monitoring stability and adoption signals, and handing over cleanly to ENGIE’s business-as-usual teams.

- Early releases and workarounds: planning for known limitations in early releases, and reflecting them in training, knowledge and communications so users are never caught by surprise. You’ll work with Release Management so each platform release arrives with the enablement it needs.

What you’ll bring 

Ideally, you’ll have:

- Several years of hands-on change delivery on large platform or systems transformations, with a recognised change management discipline. You solve a wide range of problems creatively and work with little supervision.

- Experience in regulated, customer-facing operational environments, including live customer account migration, cutover and go-live, where you have shaped the approach rather than only followed one.

- Strong communication and stakeholder management, credible with client programme leads and transformation sponsors.

- Fluency in French and English, written and spoken.

- Comfort working with data: you explore adoption and programme data yourself, report on it clearly and challenge decisions when evidence is weak.

- Commercial awareness: you understand how Kaluza makes money and balance what the client needs against cost, working alongside SI partners and the client’s own change resources without duplicating effort.

What will set you apart: a background in energy retail or utilities, vendor-side experience on a SaaS implementation, and/or knowledge of contact centre operations and technology.

Our Values 

Five values guide how we work at Kaluza:

- Play to win: Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale.

- Solve the real problem: Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes.

- Build trust every day: Consistency, transparency and doing what we say.

- Own the outcome: Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.

- Go further together: Collaboration, respect and different perspectives.

Our Perks 

- Financial & Insurance: Discretionary bonus, Alan Mutuelle Health Insurance, x3 Life & Death insurance (Prévoyance) via Alan, and standard Sécurité Sociale contributions (pension, family allowance, unemployment insurance)

- Allowances: 50% commuting expense reimbursement, €200 Home Working Allowance, and €150 Learning Fund

- Time Off & Flexibility: 25 days holiday + bank holidays + RTT days, Moments That Matter Leave, Compassionate Leave, two paid Volunteering Days, Flexible Working, and Career Break eligibility

Come as you are 

We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you.

Find out more on our careers page and LinkedIn . Our Applicant Data Protection Policy is here .

Compensation: €56 – €75

title: ML Hydrologist, Flood Forecasting
description:
About the Role
Global ML flood models now outperform traditional approaches on large rivers, but they still break down in the small, fast catchments where flash floods happen. Riverkin, a VC-backed ETH Zürich Spin-off, is closing that gap. We start from hydrological models trained across thousands of catchments worldwide and make them accurate locally, using a sensor network we deploy ourselves in exactly the places public datasets don't reach.

We are looking for an ML hydrologist to own that work. You will report to the CTO and work directly with our other hydrologist, who covers rainfall radar and short-term nowcasting.

Why this is interesting 

- Data nobody else has: Our own field-deployed sensors give you live streamflow observations in small, previously ungauged catchments.

- An open problem: Whether large-sample models can be made reliable at flash-flood scale is unsolved, and you would be working on it with real data and real users.

- Built to protect lives and critical infrastructure: Your models will power early flood warning systems safeguarding hydropower plants and giving first responders more time to protect communities

- Publishing and open source: We encourage publishing results and contributing to open tools such as NeuralHydrology and Caravan.

- Compute: GPU resources are available for training and experimentation.

What You'll Do 

- Bring global flood models to the local scale

- Take state-of-the-art hydrological ML models (LSTMs, Transformers) trained on large-sample datasets and adapt them to the catchments our customers care about.

- Use our own sensor data alongside public gauge, reanalysis and radar data to fine-tune and validate those models locally.

- Tackle prediction in ungauged and data-scarce basins through transfer learning and regionalisation.

- Own hydrological modelling end to end: set the technical direction, decide when to adapt pre-trained models or train our own, and lead the work from experimentation through validation to production.

- Work as one modelling team

- Make practical trade-offs between forecast accuracy, model complexity and development effort to build a reliable product that meets customer needs.

- Work side by side with our hydrologist specialising in rainfall radar and nowcasting to directly integrate rainfall nowcasts into your flood models.

- Work with software engineers to put models into production and monitor their performance.

- Identify and test advances in ML flood forecasting, turning promising research into more accurate and reliable forecasts for our customers.

- Stay close to the real world

- We believe the best modellers understand the world behind their models. We encourage you to join field deployments and customer conversations to build that understanding firsthand.

- You are an opinionated contributor to key technical decisions.

Who You Are 

- You’ve built and validated hydrological ML models across many catchments and have experience taking modelling work into real-world use.

- You combine scientific rigour with product judgement: you test assumptions, understand uncertainty and focus on improvements that matter to customers.

- You take ownership from an open question to a working solution. You set priorities, make decisions and keep moving without waiting for perfect information.

- You care deeply about the quality of your work. You dig into why models fail, follow problems through and stay invested in how your forecasts perform after deployment.

- You communicate clearly in writing and in person, can explain your reasoning and trade-offs, and work closely with people across hydrology, software, hardware and field operations.

Technical Requirements 

- Hands-on experience training or fine-tuning ML streamflow or flood models across many catchments at once (regional, continental or global), for example on CAMELS or Caravan. Experience with single-catchment models alone is not sufficient.

- Experience transferring such models to new or data-scarce catchments through fine-tuning, regionalisation, or prediction in ungauged basins.

- Strong understanding of rainfall-runoff processes and the limitations of hydrological observations and input data.

title: Senior Airspace Engineer
description:
About Electra 

Air travel is about to become something more: more direct, more accessible, and more connected to the places where people live, work and want to be. Every day in the U.S., people make 35 million trips of 50–500 miles, stuck in traffic or routed through crowded hubs. Chances are, you've been one of them. At Electra, we're changing that with the EL9, a nine-passenger, hybrid-electric aircraft that takes off and lands in just 150 feet. Our Ultra Short technology opens up thousands of new places to fly, beyond conventional runways, congested airports and long drives. We're backed by Lockheed Martin, Honeywell and Safran. Operators worldwide have signed intent-to-purchase agreements for the first 2,200 aircraft we produce, and we're moving toward first test flights in 2027. 

Getting a new kind of aircraft airborne takes more than ambition. It takes our kind of bold: people who think big while working in the real world. Who move ideas into action and collaborate without silos. Who put people first and make room at the table for everyone. Who challenge one another without diminishing one another. 

Sound like you? Then look beyond what you thought were your own limits, and help us take flight beyond runways. 

The Role 

Electra.aero is seeking an experienced Senior Airspace Engineer to develop the methods, operational concepts, procedures, airspace solutions, and policies needed to safely integrate Ultra Short operations into the national airspace system, including at major airports and novel, distributed access points. 

The engineer will shape flight demonstrations, tabletop exercises, simulations, and data collection to inform Ultra Short policy, guidance, and standards development in the US and Europe. Collaboration with the FAA, NATCA, and industry standards development organizations is central to the role. 

This role requires a deep understanding of how aircraft performance, flight operations, airspace design, VFR/IFR procedures, PBN, RNAV/RNP operations, obstacle evaluation, navigation systems, FAA/EASA regulations, and real-world operational constraints intersect. The successful candidate will translate new aircraft capabilities and operational concepts into safe, certifiable, and operationally useful flight-path infrastructure. 

The ideal candidate understands airspace design and air traffic management concepts, tools, and workflows across congested terminal and en route airspace, and has led or contributed to research translating novel aircraft capabilities into operational procedures. They are comfortable working directly with the FAA, international civil aviation authorities, air navigation service providers, airport authorities, and local stakeholders to advance integration projects. Firsthand experience in procedure design, airspace design, or air traffic control is valuable; working familiarity with the FAA’s 8260-series Orders is expected. 

The engineer will collaborate with Electra and FAA teams through Electra’s Cooperative Research and Development Agreement (CRADA) with the FAA Tech Center, the FAA eIPP program, the Virginia Smart Airspace Program, and the International Test Arena in Norway, as well as through company-led testing and procedure development. 

What You’ll Do 

- Translate EL9 performance characteristics into Ultra Short operational capabilities, including ground footprint, obstacle clearance, and maneuvering. 

- Collaborate with aircraft performance engineers to model EL9 capabilities under normal, degraded, and contingency conditions, incorporating system safety analysis to define feasible Ultra Short procedures. 

- Develop candidate procedures for novel urban access points and existing airports, taking into account EL2/EL9 Ultra Short performance, instrument procedure design criteria, airport traffic flows, and the obstacle environment. 

- Review FAA, EASA, ICAO, and national standards—including fixed-wing, heliport, and vertiport frameworks, FAA 8260-series Orders, and international equivalents—to identify regulatory and policy gaps affecting proposed procedures. 

- Evaluate candidate procedures with Electra’s product team, the FAA, airport operations teams, and local air traffic control to prepare for flight demonstrations, tabletop exercises, simulations, and future policy and standards development. 

- Define learning objectives and data collection requirements for flight demonstrations and simulations to validate operational concepts. 

- Synthesize flight test results, lessons learned, and operational insights to inform regulatory workstreams developing Ultra Short policy and standards. 

- Support Electra’s commercial and infrastructure partnerships teams in assessing the feasibility of candidate access points in urban settings and at airports. 

- Develop thought leadership materials that clearly explain novel Ultra Short operational concepts to regulators, local stakeholders, and airport authorities. 

- Represent Electra in FAA, EASA, and ICAO working groups and industry standards development organizations to help shape standards, guidance, and policy for Ultra Short airspace integration and operations. 

What you Bring 

- Master’s degree or PhD in aerospace engineering, aviation management, airport planning, or a related field. 

- 5+ years of experience in airspace management research, policy and regulatory development, airspace or procedure design, or a related domain. 

- Strong working knowledge of FAA and/or EASA regulatory frameworks, including the AC 150 series, Part 135, Part 23, TERPS/PANS-OPS, 8260-series Orders, and relevant airport design standards. 

- Experience working with regulators, air navigation service providers, airport operators, and industry partners. 

- Strong technical writing and verbal communication skills. 

- Ability to thrive in a fast-moving, entrepreneurial environment with evolving requirements and limited precedent. 

Bonus Points 

- Experience leading or contributing to airspace integration research, including FAA, NASA, or MITRE airspace modernization initiatives. 

- Experience as an air traffic controller or with a non-FAA service provider specializing in instrument procedure design and development. 

- Private or commercial pilot experience. 

What We Offer 

- Medical, dental, and vision insurance; STD, LTD, and life insurance 

- Generous PTO, sick leave, and company holidays 

- Paid winter break 

- 401(k) with immediate vesting 

- Free catered lunches, coffee, snacks, and drinks at our Manassas headquarters 

- Free on-site parking

title: Programmatic Advertising Specialist - BENELUX
description:
Programmatic Advertising Specialist (Dutch Speaking)

Publisher Success | Amsterdam, Netherlands (Onsite) | Full Time | Permanent 

About Refinery89

Refinery89 is a Dutch AdTech company headquartered in Madrid, working with premium publishers worldwide to optimize programmatic advertising performance.

Through advanced, data-driven technology, we help publishers maximize advertising revenue, improve monetization efficiency, and gain greater transparency across their advertising operations.

Our international team brings together specialists in programmatic advertising, publisher monetization, technology, and account management to deliver measurable results for our partners.

About the Role

Are you currently working in Programmatic Advertising, Ad Operations, Campaign Management, or Publisher Monetization and looking to take the next step in your career?

We're looking for a Dutch-speaking Programmatic Advertising Specialist to join our Publisher Success team in Amsterdam.

This opportunity is ideal for someone with a solid understanding of digital advertising who wants to move beyond campaign execution and take on a more strategic, publisher-facing role.

You don't need previous Account Management experience. We're particularly interested in candidates who understand the programmatic advertising ecosystem, enjoy analyzing performance, solving technical challenges, and communicating with clients.

You'll work directly with Dutch publishers, helping them optimize their advertising performance, maximize revenue, and develop long-term partnerships with Refinery89.

You'll collaborate closely with our Technical Account Managers, AdTech specialists, Product, and Sales teams to deliver the best possible experience for our publishing partners.

Key Responsibilities

Publisher Relationship Management

- Build and maintain strong relationships with publishers in the Netherlands.
- Serve as a primary point of contact for publisher inquiries, performance discussions, and ongoing support.
- Develop a deep understanding of each publisher's business needs and monetization objectives.
- Build trust through proactive communication, responsiveness, and problem-solving.

Programmatic Performance & Revenue Optimization

- Monitor and analyze advertising performance, including revenue, eCPM, fill rates, and other relevant programmatic metrics.
- Identify opportunities to improve publisher monetization and overall advertising performance.
- Translate advertising data into clear insights and actionable recommendations.
- Collaborate with technical specialists to implement and evaluate optimization initiatives.

Technical Coordination & Troubleshooting

- Help publishers identify and resolve advertising-related issues.
- Work closely with internal AdTech and Technical Account Management teams to investigate technical challenges.
- Coordinate solutions and ensure publishers receive timely updates.
- Develop a strong understanding of Refinery89's advertising technology and monetization solutions.

Strategic Growth & Publisher Success

- Identify opportunities to grow existing publisher accounts.
- Support publisher performance reviews and strategic discussions.
- Share insights about market trends, advertising technologies, and monetization opportunities.
- Contribute to long-term publisher satisfaction, retention, and growth.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

- Work closely with Publisher Sales, Technical Account Managers, AdTech, Product, and Finance teams.
- Communicate publisher feedback and market insights internally.
- Help improve processes, workflows, and the overall publisher experience.

What We're Looking For

Must-Have Qualifications

- Native-level Dutch proficiency , with professional working proficiency in English.
- 1 to 3 years of experience in programmatic advertising, AdTech, digital advertising, campaign management, or publisher operations.
- Familiarity with the programmatic advertising ecosystem, including technologies such as Google Ad Manager, SSPs, DSPs, or ad exchanges.
- Comfortable working with advertising performance data, reports, and dashboards.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Excellent communication skills and the ability to explain technical concepts clearly.
- Proactive, organized, and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment.
- Interest in working directly with publishers and developing long-term business relationships.

Nice to Have

- Experience with Google Ad Manager or other advertising platforms.
- Knowledge of header bidding, Prebid.js, or publisher monetization strategies.
- Previous experience working with publishers, media owners, or advertising technology companies.
- Experience in campaign optimization, yield management, or programmatic trading.
- Previous client-facing or Account Management experience.

Previous Account Management experience is NOT required. 

Who Should Apply?

We encourage applications from professionals currently working in roles such as:

- Programmatic Advertising Specialist
- Programmatic Trader
- Ad Operations Specialist
- Campaign Manager (Programmatic)
- Publisher Operations Specialist
- Yield Optimization Specialist
- Digital Advertising Specialist
- Technical Account Specialist (AdTech)

If you have a technical understanding of digital advertising and want to develop your career in publisher relationship management, we'd love to hear from you.

Why Join Refinery89?

- Work at a growing international AdTech company with Dutch roots.
- Develop expertise in publisher monetization and programmatic advertising.
- Transition into a more strategic, client-facing position while building on your existing technical knowledge.
- Collaborate with experienced AdTech professionals across multiple departments.
- Gain exposure to premium publishers and advanced advertising technologies.
- Build your career in a dynamic and rapidly evolving industry.

Interview Process

Our recruitment process consists of four stages:

- Initial Screening: Introductory call with our Talent Acquisition team.
- First Interview: Video interview with members of the Publisher Success team.
- Second Interview: Interview with the Hiring Manager and/or senior stakeholders.
- Final Interview: In-person meeting with the Hiring Manager and key team members (location to be confirmed).

title: Campaign Analyst
description:
Onze missie is helder: beter eten voor meer mensen bereikbaar maken. Als Campaign Analyst in het Customer Retention team speel je hierin een cruciale rol door onze klanten beter vast te houden. Jij zorgt ervoor dat we al onze verhalen, over al onze producten, op de juiste manier aan de juiste klant vertellen. Je bent continu, datagedreven op zoek naar verbetering; zodat we het volgende verhaal nóg beter vertellen.

Wat je gaat doen

Onze retentiestrategie wordt steeds geavanceerder. We sturen niet simpelweg 'een korting' naar alle klanten maar werken met gelaagde acties, inspirerende verhalen en gepersonaliseerde extra’s.

Enerzijds ben jij de analytische drijfkracht achter de executie van onze campagnes. Je bouwt, beheert en verbetert de analytische tooling en dashboards zodat we kunnen blijven leren. Daarmee creëer je begrip van - en grip op - de commerciële impact van campagnes, en alle onderliggende onderdelen (zoals kanaalstrategie, product-samenstelling of klantdoelgroep). Vervolgens vertaal je de verworven inzichten effectief naar succesfactoren, verbeteringstrajecten en/of toekomstige experimenten. Anderzijds werk je inhoudelijk mee. Je bepaalt samen met de Campaign Specialist welk aanbod naar welke klanten gaat, via welk kanaal en met welke verwachting en zet je ook (nieuwe) acties zelf op.

Een aantal van jouw verantwoordelijkheden: 

- Je bent verantwoordelijk voor de performance van campagnes. Je analyseert de impact, en je gebruikt inzichten om toekomstige campagnes te verbeteren, zodat we kunnen blijven innoveren in onze retentiestrategie.

- Je werkt actief mee met het team: je levert niet alleen de inzichten, maar bent ook zelf verantwoordelijk voor de implementatie van campagnes.

- Je bepaalt en draait de experimentagenda: welke hypotheses testen we over aanbod, doelgroep en kanaal, en wat leren we ervan?

- Je bouwt, onderhoudt en verbetert zelf de datamodellen (SQL/dbt) en dashboards (Data Studio) waarop het team stuurt.

Dit ben jij

- Je hebt een afgeronde WO of HBO-opleiding op zak.

- Je hebt 2-5 jaar ervaring met marketing (intelligence) en data/business analytics.

- Je spreekt en schrijft vloeiend Nederlands.

- Je bent analytisch sterk en je werkt datagedreven en gestructureerd. Je kunt vloeiend SQL, hebt ervaring met het maken van dashboards en datamodellen en je gebruikt graag AI-tools om je werk efficiënter te maken. Ervaring met dbt is een pré.

- Je hebt ervaring met A/B-tests, holdout-tests en hypothese gedreven werken.

- Je hebt commercieel gevoel: je denkt net zo graag mee over het aanbod als over de cijfers erachter.

- Je bent een sterke sparringpartner: je daagt collega’s uit met data en laat je zelf ook uitdagen.

- Je bent kritisch, hands-on en niet bang om de status quo uit te dagen.

Wat wij bieden

- Werken bij een B Corp gecertificeerd bedrijf, waarbij je de kans krijgt om je stempel te drukken op het Europese voedselsysteem.

- 27 vakantiedagen om bij te komen en op te laden.

- Een extra vrije dag per jaar om je in te zetten voor vrijwilligerswerk en iets goeds te doen.

- Aandacht voor je mentale gezondheid met online begeleiding van erkende psychologen via OpenUp.

- Voor straks een perfect pensioen via BPFL.

- Elke maand food for thought, met workshops en talks via de Crisp University.

- Regelmatig tastings of workshops op kantoor of bij een van onze leveranciers, om te zien hoe onze lekkerste producten worden gemaakt – en natuurlijk ook te proeven.

- Dagelijks een uitgebreide, georganiseerde lunch op kantoor.

- Enthousiaste, slimme collega’s en tijd om elkaar te leren kennen tijdens sport, events en proeverijen.

- En... fikse korting op je Crisp boodschappen, omdat je thuis natuurlijk ook goed wilt eten.

Onze selectieprocedure

Solliciteer via onderstaande button. Hoe meer je kunt delen over jezelf en de reden dat je solliciteert, hoe beter.

Bij Crisp streven we naar een inclusieve en diverse werkomgeving waarin iedereen welkom is, ongeacht hun achtergrond, geslacht, leeftijd, etniciteit, seksuele geaardheid, religie of beperking. Wij moedigen sollicitanten met diverse perspectieven en achtergronden aan om te solliciteren en geloven in gelijke kansen voor iedereen. We waarderen de unieke bijdragen die elke medewerker kan leveren en zijn vastbesloten om een inclusieve werkplek te creëren waarin iedereen wordt gerespecteerd en gewaardeerd.

title: Enterprise Account Executive
description:
At Deeploy, we help organisations roll out AI they can trust. Banks, insurers and pharma companies have to show they control their AI use, and most don’t yet have the tooling to do so. Deeploy gives them that control. We work with dozens of enterprise customers in finance, insurance and healthcare.

You’ll own deals from first outreach to signed contract, with a focus on the Netherlands and Northwest Europe. Most of our buyers have never bought AI governance before, so much of the work is helping them define the problem and build the internal case. You report to the COO, and the founders stay involved in deals.

What you’ll do 

- Deals: run enterprise deals from qualification to close. Deals typically take 6 to 12 months and involve risk, compliance, legal, IT and a business sponsor. The GRC (governance, risk and compliance) function is often the way in.

- Pipeline: build a large part of your own pipeline through outbound, your network, our partners and events. Marketing runs campaigns with you.

- Visibility: speak at events and roundtables for risk, compliance and AI governance audiences.

- Feedback: bring back what buyers respond to, how they compare us with alternatives, and what they miss in the product.

- Process: help set up how we qualify, forecast and run deals, and later how we onboard new sellers. We’re a small team that works with AI daily, so you’ll also build some of your own tools and agents.

After 12 months 

- You’ve closed at least 4 new enterprise accounts and built €1m+ of qualified pipeline.

- AI Governance officers know Deeploy, and know you.

- You have proven to yourself as part of our team, culture and processes.

Who we’re looking for 

- You’ve closed complex enterprise deals with long cycles and several stakeholders, ideally in financial services, insurance, pharma or life sciences.

- You know how risk, compliance or IT buyers think, from selling GRC, security, data or AI software, or from working on the buyer side.

- You have a network among these buyers in the Netherlands or elsewhere in Northwest Europe.

- You can discuss the EU AI Act and how AI systems are built and monitored with some confidence. You don’t need to be an engineer.

- You’ve worked at an early-stage company or founded one, and you’re comfortable building pipeline from scratch.

- Fluent English. Dutch or German is a strong plus.

What the role is, and what it is not 

It is a builder role. Deal ownership comes first, commercial process a close second.

It is not a lead-execution seat, and you don’t carry the number alone. The founders stay close to deals and are responsible for the commercial function.

What we offer 

- Competitive base and bonus

- Share plan from day 1

- Pension plan and other benefits

- Hybrid working from The Stack in Amsterdam, home to around 40 AI startups

- The chance to be part of an early stage startup, building the sales function and grow with it

Hiring process 

- Application: your CV or LinkedIn, and something you’ve worked on that you’re proud of

- Introductory call (30 minutes)

- Conversation with two people you’d work with closely (60 minutes)

- Case study (3 hours, timeboxed), presented to two team members

- Offer

title: Model-Based Systems Engineer
description:
About Us 

QuantWare is building the world’s most powerful quantum processors to solve humanity's greatest challenges. We do this with our unique VIO™ technology, the only QPU architecture that breaks the hardware barriers that have held quantum computing back, unlocking the path to MegaQubit quantum processors.

Our Systems Integration Team is seeking a Model-Based Systems Engineer to build the tools and framework we use to design the systems that operate our VIO and QPU technology. This role is focused on establishing QuantWare’s MBSE methodology and turning knowledge from cryogenics, wiring, control electronics and software into a single, executable system model. You will define how we model our systems and build the libraries, analyses and integrations that make the model useful day to day. Working closely with processor, hardware and software teams, you will play an important role in enabling the design of the large-scale quantum computers built around VIO-powered QPUs.

What are you going to do? 

- Define and own QuantWare’s MBSE methodology, modelling conventions and architecture framework for quantum computing systems, covering the quantum processor, cryostat, signal chain, control and readout electronics, and software stack.

- Select, set up and maintain the MBSE toolchain (e.g. SysML v2, Capella or Cameo), including version control, model reviews and integration with existing engineering tools.

- Build reusable model libraries for key subsystems, including QPU interfaces, cryogenic wiring and attenuation, microwave signal paths, and control electronics.

- Develop automated analyses on top of the model, such as heat-load, signal-integrity and noise budgets, channel counts, scalability, and full-system metrics such as power consumption as qubit counts grow.

- Establish requirements traceability from customer and system-level requirements down to component specifications and verification tests.

- Connect the system model to simulation and measurement data, creating a digital thread between design and test.

- Support system architecture and trade studies for new VIO and QPU generations and customer system integrations.

- Drive adoption across the company, training and supporting engineers in using the models and tools in their day-to-day work.

Core Requirements: 

- BSc. or MSc. in systems engineering, electrical engineering, physics, mechanical engineering or a related field.

- 3+ years of hands-on MBSE experience, including building or extending a modelling framework rather than only using existing ones.

- Hands on experience with hardware system models that encompass multiple subsystems with differing requirements and interfaces.

- Strong working knowledge of SysML (v1 and/or v2) and at least one MBSE tool, such as Cameo, Capella or equivalent.

- Proficiency in Python for model automation, analysis and tool integration via APIs.

- A solid track record in requirements engineering and verification of complex, multidisciplinary hardware systems.

- Strong organisational and communication skills. You thrive in a cross-disciplinary environment and are comfortable taking ownership from day one.

- Experience with cryogenic, RF/microwave or precision instrumentation systems, or direct experience with superconducting quantum hardware.

- Background in high-tech, semiconductor, aerospace or scientific instrumentation industries.

- Experience introducing MBSE into an organisation and driving its adoption.

- Familiarity with SysML v2 APIs, digital thread concepts or co-simulation (e.g. FMI), as well as systems engineering standards such as ISO/IEC 15288.

description:

Met je brede kennis en jarenlange ervaring sta je stevig in een dynamische projectomgeving. Dat doe je niet alleen: samen schop je ‘t verder. Je werkt nauw samen met het management en de overige projectleiders over offertes, de bureauplanning en kansen in de markt.

Dit ben jij 

Je bent open, nieuwsgierig en staat als leidinggevende stevig in je schoenen. Je omgeving ziet je als collegiaal en je neemt verantwoordelijkheid over je project en de ontwikkeling van de projectteamleden.

- Een salaris tussen €4.500 – €6.900 bruto o.b.v. fulltime dienstverband, afhankelijk van je kennis en ervaring.

title: Senior Software Engineer, OS Integration
description:
Why Mozilla? 

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people. 

The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms. 

About the OS Integration team: 

The OS Integration team ensures Firefox works well with the host operating system and environment. We’re a distributed team with expertise in Windows, macOS, and Linux-based operating systems. Our responsibilities include developing fixes and improvements for Firefox related to Windows, macOS, and Linux environments. This might include integration with a new OS feature or fixing an OS-specific user interface bug. Other responsibilities include native crash reporting, OS abstraction layers, sandboxing, hardening, updater, and enterprise DLP support. 

About the role: 

As a member of the OS Integration team, you’ll develop fixes, improvements, and new features for Firefox. In many cases work may be cross-platform or have a cross-platform component. This role will include maintenance and development of the installer and updater of Firefox. You’ll contribute to the team through code review and discussion. 

What you’ll do: 

- Improve the quality of Firefox and other Mozilla products by debugging and fixing software defects, improving the browsing experience for hundreds of millions of users. 

- Contribute to new features and improvements. 

- Break down tasks and work with others to deliver solutions. 

- Collaborate with experienced software engineers. 

- Perform code reviews and provide technical direction. 

- Work with a geographically-distributed development team. 

- Interact with teams throughout the organization. 

What you’ll bring: 

- 5+ years of overall software engineering experience 

- Strong knowledge of C and C++ 

- Experience with desktop application development on Windows, macOS, or Linux with C++. 

- Knowledge of web technologies such as Javascript and HTML. 

- Knowledge of secure coding practices and memory safety concerns. 

- Strong problem-solving and debugging skills. 

- Written and verbal communication skills with a collaborative mindset. 

- Willingness to work effectively in a distributed team environment. 

- Commitment to our values: 

- Play to win 

- Build for People first 

- Engage Evidence over Ego 

- Decide and Deliver 

- Ship, learn and repeat 

Bonus Points for experience with: 

- Installer and/or Updater development on any OS 

- Windows internals like the BITS server or MSIX packages 

- Open-source contributions or personal engineering projects 

What you’ll get: 

- Generous performance-based bonus plans to all eligible employees - we share in our success as one team 

- Rich medical, dental, and vision coverage 

- Generous retirement contributions with 100% immediate vesting (regardless of whether you contribute) 

- Quarterly all-company wellness days where everyone takes a pause together 

- Country specific holidays plus a day off for your birthday 

- One-time home office stipend 

- Annual professional development budget 

- Considerable paid parental leave 

- Employee referral bonus program 

- Other benefits (life/AD&D, disability, EAP, etc. - varies by country) 

About Mozilla 

Mozilla exists to build the Internet as a public resource accessible to all because we believe that open and free is better than closed and controlled. When you work at Mozilla, you give yourself a chance to make a difference in the lives of Web users everywhere. And you give us a chance to make a difference in your life every single day. Join us to work on the Web as the platform and help create more opportunity and innovation for everyone online.

title: Senior Integration Software Engineer
description:
We are looking for an experienced Senior Integration Software Engineer to bring our algorithms and software backend together into reliable, operational solutions, and to take technical ownership of how our software is integrated.

Optics11 is a deep-tech company developing advanced fiber-optic sensing technologies for challenging environments and applications in energy and underwater security. Our systems enable high-performance sensing and monitoring through advanced photonics, signal processing, and data-driven intelligence.

We are expanding our R&D team with an Integration Software Engineer who enjoys building clean, reliable interfaces between components and working where software meets hardware, and who takes ownership of making complex systems work together end to end.

As a Senior Integration Software Engineer, you will support their integration into operational systems: connecting algorithms to the backend through robust APIs, building data connectors, health reporting and control software, and defining and verifying integrations with Command and Control (C2) systems.

You will work closely with domain experts in acoustics, signal processing and machine learning, and with the software engineering team, and hands-on with our monitoring systems at our headquarters and production facility. You will also take technical ownership of work delivered by internal and external engineers and set the standard for good engineering practices.

Key Responsibilities 

- Lead software integration engineering for our underwater acoustic sensing systems, ensuring frontend and backend components, algorithms, and hardware systems work together reliably.

- Integrate the algorithmic toolbox with our system backends, turning research code into maintainable, versioned and deployable software components.

- Implement data interfaces for our real-time sonar processing pipeline, to ingest multiple sensors (acoustic, heading, temperature, pressure, etc.) from internal and external data acquisition systems. Implement health reporting, logging and monitoring, so that the status and performance of software and system components is visible and actionable.

- Develop the software control layer for our sensing systems and their hardware components, including APIs for commanding, state handling, error handling and recovery.

- Implement, align and verify software integrations with external partners and C2 systems, being directly involved in defining interfaces, maintaining interface specifications and running joint integration tests.

- Testing & debugging: Develop system-level test suites and CI/CD pipelines, diagnose communication failures, and ensure secure, reliable data transfers as the toolbox and backends evolve.

- Address performance, latency and scalability of the integrated pipeline, together with algorithm and backend developers.

- Work hands-on with integrated software and hardware systems at our headquarters and production facility, with occasional on-site visits.

- Review the work of junior engineers and external development partners in depth, promote good practices for packaging, versioning and release, and share integration knowledge across the team.

Why Join Us? 

- Join one of Europe’s most promising deep-tech scale-ups.

- Shape the future of a rapidly growing multidisciplinary R&D organization.

- Competitive salary and benefits package.

- Enjoy regular team activities and company events.

- Fresh team lunches provided 5 times/week.

Qualifications:

- BSc or MSc in Computer Science, Software Engineering or a related field.

- Significant professional experience in software engineering, with a focus on system integration, backend or platform development.

- Extensive experience developing production software in Python, including packaging, testing, dependency management and writing maintainable, well-structured code.

- Familiarity with systems programming in C++, or Rust, for the purpose of extending Python for more performance or hardware control.

- Proven experience designing and implementing APIs and messaging interfaces (e.g. MQTT, WebSocket) and data serialization (e.g. protobuf).

- Experience with realtime data pipelines, and handling high-throughput or streaming data.

- Experience with Docker, CI/CD and automated testing in a Linux environment.

- Experience working with software that interacts with physical systems, and comfort doing hands-on integration and troubleshooting in a lab or production environment.

- Experience reviewing code and designs, mentoring junior engineers, and setting engineering standards.

- An outcome-focused mindset, with the ability to own a problem end to end or break it down for others.

- Ability to work with algorithm developers and translate research code into robust, maintainable software.

- Flexible and proactive in taking on what needs to be addressed, and comfortable in a fast-paced scale-up environment.

- Good communication skills in English and the ability to coordinate with internal teams and external partners.

- Willingness to work primarily from our Amsterdam headquarters, as parts of the role involve classified information and physical systems.

Nice to Have:

- Knowledge of defense systems or defense standards (e.g. NATO STANAGs, MIL-STD), for example in naval, maritime security or surveillance systems.

- Experience with the scientific Python stack (e.g. NumPy, SciPy) or integrating signal processing or ML models into production systems.

- Experience developing software interfaces for controlling instruments or devices.

- Experience with other messaging or streaming frameworks (e.g. Kafka, ZeroMQ, DDS).

- Familiarity with observability tooling.

Security & Compliance: 

You'll be working with clients in the defense and security sectors, obtaining a Certificate of No Objection issued by the AIVD (Dutch General Intelligence and Security Service) is mandatory. This means you will need to undergo a security screening. For more information, please refer to details on security screening.

title: Senior Medewerker Finance & Accounting
description:

Als Boekhoudkundig Medewerker ben je verantwoordelijk voor een correcte en tijdige verwerking van de financiële administratie. Je houdt je bezig met debiteuren, crediteuren, cashmanagement en grootboekcontroles. Daarnaast bereid je de maand- en jaarafsluiting voor en werk je nauw samen met de Financial Controller en andere collega's binnen Finance. - Debiteuren- en crediteurenbeheer: Je beheert de openstaande posten, verwerkt ontvangsten en inkoopfacturen en onderhoudt contact met klanten en leveranciers over betalingen en factuurverschillen.

- Cashmanagement: Je verwerkt bankmutaties, bewaakt de geldstromen en bereidt betalingen voor. Ook ondersteun je bij de liquiditeitsplanning.

- Referentiecheck (na jouw goedkeuring)/ assessment

title: Werkstudent Medisch Acceptatie
description:
Over ons 

Europa verandert. Steeds meer mensen kiezen voor vrijheid — als zzp'er, freelancer of ondernemer. Ze bepalen zelf wanneer, hoe en met wie ze werken. Maar die vrijheid komt met een keerzijde: onzekerheid.

Bij Insify geloven we dat ondernemers zich geen zorgen moeten maken over verzekeringen. Daarom bouwen we iets wat de verzekeringswereld hard nodig heeft: transparante, eerlijke en volledig digitale verzekeringen, speciaal voor mensen die voor zichzelf werken. Geen ingewikkeld papierwerk, geen gedoe. Vandaag geregeld, morgen verzekerd.

We verzekeren inmiddels duizenden klanten in heel Europa — en we zijn nog maar net begonnen.

Het Operations Team 

Wij zijn het gezicht van Insify. Bij elk telefoontje, elke e-mail en elk gesprek bouwen we vertrouwen op. We zorgen ervoor dat klanten zich gehoord, gesteund en goed geholpen voelen — ook als het ingewikkeld wordt. Snelheid en kwaliteit gaan bij ons hand in hand, en we verbeteren continu op basis van wat we leren. Met een groeiend medisch acceptatieteam en uitbreiding naar meerdere Europese landen, speel jij een directe rol in iets wat echt impact maakt.

Jouw rol 

Als Medisch Acceptatie Werkstudent ben jij het eerste aanspreekpunt voor onze klanten in een van de meest persoonlijke momenten van hun ondernemerschap. Je werkt nauw samen met medische specialisten en zorgt ervoor dat aanvragen soepel, nauwkeurig en klantgericht verlopen. Dit is geen standaard bijbaan — je draait mee in een snel groeiend team waar jouw bijdrage echt telt.

Wat ga je doen 

- Klantcontact. Je beantwoordt vragen via telefoon, e-mail en chat. Je legt complexe verzekeringspolissen en medische beslissingen uit op een manier die klanten écht begrijpen.

- Gegevensbeheer. Je vraagt medische dossiers op bij huisartsen en specialisten, controleert de volledigheid en verwerkt alles nauwkeurig in ons systeem.

- Samenwerken met specialisten. Je fungeert als schakel tussen de klant en de medisch specialist — je vat informatie samen, signaleert complexe vraagstukken en houdt de communicatie helder.

- Administratie. Je houdt klantgegevens up-to-date, verwerkt poliswijzigingen en bewaakt deadlines.

Wat je meebrengt

title: Insurance Product Manager / Underwriter (P&C)
description:
Most insurance product roles ask you to perfect one product in one market. This one asks you to build Europe’s SME insurance products: decide what we cover and who we insure, negotiate it with our carriers and get it live, market after market.

Deep in the wording. Fast in the build. 

About Insify 

Insurance for entrepreneurs is still built the old way: one market at a time, wordings nobody reads, and cover that leaves out the very businesses that need it most.

We're doing it differently.

Insify is a high-growth scale-up backed by €43M in total funding from world-class investors like Accel, Munich Re Ventures, and Formula 1 champion Nico Rosberg. In five years, we've expanded from the Netherlands into France, Germany and Ireland, and we're just getting started. Our mission: become the European leader in AI-powered SME insurance.

We aren't just building a company; we're leading a revolution. Our culture is intense, high-stakes, and mission-driven. We hire smart, ambitious "owners" who possess a relentless drive to win. This is an environment for those who thrive on challenges, value intellectual honesty, and share our mindset of becoming a global category leader.

Our founding team consists of seasoned entrepreneurs who have previously built iconic businesses like HelloFresh, Bloomon, and SumUp. We bring that same bias for speed, scale, and high standards to one of the most structurally broken experiences in financial services. Together, we combine that deep fintech and e-commerce expertise with cutting-edge AI to stay ahead of the curve.

What you’ll own in your first year 
You won’t inherit a finished product shelf. You’ll build the engine that fills it.

- Build the product engine. Turn how we benchmark a market into a system: compare cover, limits and exclusions across local players, our Dutch home product and our other markets, so every new product starts from facts, not gut feeling.

- Make the call on cover. Decide what we cover, what we don’t and who we insure, and turn it into a proposal. The tools do the comparison; the judgment is yours.

- Get it signed. Take the proposal to our risk carriers and negotiate it. You know what to push on, what to let go and which clause will set off six red flags.

- Get it live. Adapt our wordings to each new market, run the legal review and launch. Less writing from scratch, more making one strong product fit the next market. Then track loss ratios, competition and customer feedback, and sharpen it.

- Build what doesn’t exist yet. In the markets where we double down, own custom products from the insurance side, including cover for the trades and businesses others decline.

Who you are 
You’re an insurance expert first and a builder second, but a real one.

- You have 5+ years hands-on in commercial P&C (Property & Casualty) at an insurer, MGA, (re)insurer or specialist broker, across underwriting, product and wordings, ideally for SMEs.

- You know what is covered, what isn’t and what should be . Hand you a wording from a market you’ve never worked in and you’ll spot the gaps within minutes.

- You’ve worked across more than one line, product or market , and you can apply what you know to a market you’ve never seen.

- You’ve sat at the table with insurers or capacity providers and know where the red lines are.

- You’d rather fix insurance than complain about it. Maybe you already tried: at an insurtech, an MGA, your own startup, or on the carrier side building products with insurtechs.

- You think like the customer : plain questions, fair cover, and no excluding everything just to be safe.

- You’re at home in Excel and data , and curious about what automation and LLMs can take off your plate. You don’t need to code; our product and tech teams build the digital journey with you.

- You work fluently in English ; German, French or Dutch is a big plus.

What we offer 

- Real ownership. You decide what we cover and work directly with the MT, close to where decisions get made.

- Range. More products and markets in a year than most people see in a decade at an incumbent.

- A share in what we build. Equity, so you share in the value you build.

- A team that cares. We live by four values: Grit, Care, Impact and Entrepreneurship.

- Growth. Room to grow into leading our insurance product work as we add markets, plus an in-house coaching and leadership program.

- The package. Competitive salary package + 6% pension, holidays, well-being budget and rich social events (ski trip, summer and winter party).

- The basics, done well. Office in central Amsterdam, laptop, hybrid working. Relocation support.

If you know insurance inside out and you’d rather build products than maintain them, we’d like to meet you. No cover letter needed.

title: Senior Business Controller (Operations)
description:
Would you like to work closely with the business as a Senior Business Controller and use your financial expertise to make a real impact on decisions? You will bring financial structure and insight, while keeping a forward-looking perspective: where can we improve, which decisions will make a financial difference, and what will they mean for our results? 

HG is a compact, international organisation. This means considerable responsibility, direct contact with decision-makers and room to drive change yourself. We are therefore looking for someone who takes ownership, works pragmatically and is not afraid to challenge existing ways of working. 

You will be based at our head office in Almere. Hybrid working opportunities are limited: regular office attendance is important in this role because of the close collaboration with Finance, Operations and other stakeholders. You will also travel to the United Kingdom or Germany several times a year. 

About the role 

As Senior Business Controller, you will be responsible for business control within Operations and will also support our subsidiaries in the United Kingdom and Germany. You have a clear vision of what the best operational business control model looks like and have proven experience in realizing this. The Senior Business Controller plays a key role in strengthening financial control, transparency and decision-making across Operations. The scope covers procurement and product costing, as well as warehouse and transport operations. Working closely with Finance, Procurement and Operations, the Senior Business Controller translates operational developments and improvement initiatives into clear financial insights and P&L impact 

Our business is undergoing significant change. HG has recently changed its logistics service arrangements, consolidating most local warehouses into one central location as part of a cost-saving initiative. At the same time, a new ERP system is being implemented. This creates an interesting and dynamic environment in which existing budget models, cost allocation models, reporting and financial processes need to be further developed to reflect the new operating model and provide a solid basis for financial control and decision-making. 

What you will do 

Your responsibilities will include: 

- Owning the operational cost lines between Net Sales and Contribution Margin for the whole group and . act as a strong Finance business partner to the Chief Operating Officer and his team, translating operational developments into actionable financial insights; 

- Identifying and driving continuous improvements to the operational business, improving insights while reducing costs.

- E stablish or improve proper accounting entries together with Finance Administration and relevant operational partners. 

- Co-lead the annual budget cycle and budget presentations to the Board. 

- Using and improving Power BI, ERP data and financial processes to reduce manual work and increase transparency.

This position requires more than strong analytical skills. You will need to explain your insights clearly, engage stakeholders and constructively challenge where necessary. You will be a knowledgeable sparring partner who asks questions, brings structure and takes responsibility from analysis through to implementation. You proactively identify opportunities to improve financial processes, controls, reporting and transparency across Operations. 

HG is a compact, fast-growing and international organization where you can directly see the impact of your work. This requires ownership, initiative and a pragmatic, results-oriented mindset. The team culture is open, pragmatic and focused on results, encouraging you to bring ideas forward, challenge constructively and take responsibility. Everything we do is guided by our three core values: Aim High, Be Brave, Be Connected. 

What you bring 

We are looking for a financially strong, hands-on and improvement-oriented controller who combines analytical capability with a practical understanding of Operations. The ideal candidate is comfortable working across Finance, Procurement and Operations and is able to turn complex cost drivers into clear insights and concrete actions. 

You bring a proactive mindset, strong stakeholder-management skills and a natural drive to simplify and improve processes. You are comfortable challenging existing ways of working, creating structure in a changing environment and taking ownership from analysis through implementation. 

You will also have: 

- A completed university master’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business Administration or a related field. A Registered Controller (RC) qualification is a strong advantage. 

- Around 10 years of relevant experience in business control, operations control or a comparable financial role. 

- Experience in a manufacturing environment is important, including knowledge of production processes, procurement and cost calculations. 

- A sound understanding of business control, financial controls and treasury. 

- Experience with ERP systems and an understanding of how financial data and accounting flows are structured. 

- Good knowledge of Power BI. You do not need to build everything from scratch, but you can independently investigate, improve and develop analyses. 

- Experience working with consolidation tools. 

- Strong analytical, communication and stakeholder management skills. 

- A proactive, hands-on and improvement-oriented mindset, with the ability to create structure in a changing environment. 

- Fluency in English. Knowledge of Dutch is desirable, and German is an advantage. 

- Experience with AI tools, such as Copilot. 

- Willingness to travel to the United Kingdom and Germany several times a year. 

Please note that we do not offer visa or work permit sponsorship for this position. You must therefore hold a valid EU work permit 

What do we offer 

At HG, you will not be stepping into a role where everything is already set in stone. Changes in our logistics operations, systems and reporting create opportunities to further professionalize financial control and implement improvements yourself. 

You can expect: 

- a senior role with broad responsibility and direct influence on financial and operational decision-making; 

- a salary appropriate to the seniority of the role, with an indicative range of €85,000 to €100,000 gross per year; 

- an annual on-target bonus of 25% of your gross annual salary; 

- full-time employment with 30 days of annual leave; 

- a pension scheme; 

- a commuting allowance; 

- a full-time role based at our head office in Almere. Hybrid working is possible on a limited basis, with office attendance being an important part of the role; 

- a dynamic and ambitious working environment where initiative and ownership are valued; 

- a friendly, welcoming team, with a free shared lunch every Monday and monthly social drinks. 

We are HG 

HG is a leading European brand in specialist cleaning and maintenance products. 

We believe a home should be a place where people can live carefree, with confidence in the products they use to care for the spaces and belongings around them. Our products are developed to do exactly what they promise: deliver effective, reliable and specialist cleaning solutions that help consumers solve real household problems. 

HG’s mission is to help people enjoy their homes without worrying about what might go wrong. We do this through high-quality products, specialist expertise, clear advice and a relentless focus on performance. 

We are dedicated to delivering superiority, innovation, quality and customer satisfaction. With a strong presence across Europe and beyond, we are continuously investing to make an even bigger impact. 

HG does what it promises.

Our colleague Ilse de Groot, Corporate Recruiter, will be happy to answer any questions. You can contact her at .

title: Senior Software Engineer (.NET Ecosystem)
description:
About the team 

The Integrations Ecosystem org builds the drivers, SDKs, connectors and BI integrations that make ClickHouse feel native in any stack. The Language Clients team maintains the official clients for Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, Rust, C++ and C#, plus the ODBC, JDBC and ADBC drivers. We're small, senior and remote across North America and EMEA. Each client has a primary owner, but no client belongs to one person: we review and co-maintain across languages and decide cross-client questions together.

The role 

We're looking for a product-minded engineer to own the ClickHouse .NET client. You'll decide what the client should do by talking to the developers who use it, reading the issues and the telemetry, and listening to the community. Then you'll build it, with deep .NET expertise, and measure whether it worked. Your scope is the SDK and what builds on it: ADO.NET , Dapper and Entity Framework Core users, and the tools and integrations that depend on your client.

What you'll do 

- Know who uses the client and what they're trying to do. Define what good looks like (time to first query, error clarity, adoption by key integrations), measure it, and let that drive the roadmap.

- Be the voice of ClickHouse for .NET developers. Speak at .NET conferences and meet-ups, and write the posts, tutorials and samples that developers and AI assistants find when they search for how to use ClickHouse from .NET (SEO and GEO). Answer questions where the community asks them.

- Own the .NET client and its ecosystem: the client, the EF Core provider and ORM integrations, NuGet releases and support. Evolve it without breaking the people who depend on it.

- Review and co-maintain other clients, and take part in cross-client decisions on types, errors and protocol features.

- Bring what .NET and Windows users need to the ODBC driver, since that's how many Windows and BI tools reach ClickHouse. If you write C++, contribute to it directly.

- Bring written proposals about where we invest next. You set direction rather than wait for it.

- Make the client enterprise-ready: TLS and certificate handling, authentication including Microsoft Entra ID, safe credential handling, signed and reproducible packages, and the audit and compliance questions large .NET shops ask before they adopt.

- Shape the client for agents as users: an API, docs and error messages an AI coding agent can use correctly on the first try.

- Extend our AI development platform, with new workflows for maintaining the clients: consistency checks across languages, issue triage, release checks.

About you 

- Product-minded. You decide what to build from user evidence, measure whether it worked, and can explain what you chose not to build.

- 5+ years in software, much of it on data-intensive systems: drivers, SDKs, data access, ingestion or analytics.

- Deep C# and .NET expertise: memory management, async and the TPL, Span and pooling, profiling and benchmarking. You reason about throughput and latency down to allocations and bytes on the wire, and you prove it with tests and benchmarks.

- Fluent in C#, and productive in at least one more of our client languages (Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, Rust, C++). You'll review and co-own across clients, not only .NET.

- You've built or substantially extended a library other engineers depend on, and shipped NuGet packages across .NET Framework and modern .NET. You treat breaking changes accordingly.

- Fluent in .NET data access ( ADO.NET , Dapper, EF Core) and at home in the wider .NET ecosystem: ASP.NET Core, Aspire, NuGet.

- Security-minded. You've shipped a library into enterprise environments and know what security, compliance and procurement teams look for in a dependency.

- Enthusiastic about working in public. You've given talks or written technical content, or you're keen to, and you see it as part of the job rather than a distraction from it.

- Thoughtful use of AI development tools, with the judgment to review what comes out.

- Clear writing. Most coordination happens in design docs, PRs and RFCs.

Nice to have 

- ClickHouse, especially its type system, or another OLAP engine.

- C++ and ODBC driver internals.

- Building or maintaining an ADO.NET or EF Core provider.

- Open-source contributions to .NET or data infrastructure.

- Experience designing SDKs, docs or error messages with AI coding agents as the consumer.

- Protocol or wire-format work on a database driver or network client.

Learn more 

- Introducing the (blazing fast!) native TCP client for .NET : zero-copy columnar reads, 1.5 to 2x faster than HTTP, over 99% fewer GC allocations (Oct 2026)

- What's new in the ClickHouse .NET Driver: the road from 1.0 to 1.3 (Aug 2026)

- Meet GroeneAI: our autonomous contributor to ClickHouse (Oct 2026)

- Building a .NET API Gateway with ClickHouse and Aspire (Jun 2026)

- The .NET client on GitHub and its documentation 

- ClickHouse Workload for Microsoft Fabric, now in public preview (Sep 2026)

Perks 

- Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

- Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

- Equity in the company - Every new eligible team member who joins our company receives equity.

- Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

- A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.

- Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.

Culture - We All Shape It

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here . Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse.

title: Human Factors Project Manager (m/f/d) (part-time contractor, 3-month review)
description:
About Hilo by Aktiia 

High blood pressure is the world's most common disease, causing 18M deaths each year. At Hilo by Aktiia, we're building a world where no lives are lost to its effects — with technology that helps people take control of their health. 

We're a venture-backed scale-up with $96M raised from investors in Europe and the US. Rooted in 18 years of research at the Swiss Center for Electronics and Microtechnology (CSEM), our device is the world's only medically accurate, cuffless, continuous blood pressure monitor for daily use — clinically validated and CE Marked as a Class IIa medical device, now available in 12 countries. In July, we launched in the US. 

We're a remote-first company headquartered in Neuchâtel, Switzerland, united by our passion for impact and innovation. Applicants must already hold a valid visa or work permit for their country of residence, as Hilo is not able to provide visa sponsorship.

About the role 
Hilo is looking for an experienced Human Factors Project Manager to own all of our human factors and usability work. Right now that work is split across Product, Design, Clinical Operations, QARA and outside agencies, and no single person is accountable for it. You'll be that person. You'll coordinate the specialists, keep work moving between teams and make sure every deliverable meets the quality and regulatory standard. That frees our domain teams to get back to their own work.

What you'll own 

- Usability studies: You'll own the study calendar, protocols and relationships with external labs such as Sage Research. This covers formative and summative studies across hardware and software, including FDA submission work for Hilo Medical. You'll make sure findings get back to design on a regular schedule.
- IFU and Quick Start Guide: You'll decide what content goes in the QSG, the app and the IFU. You'll also own version control and localisation (Phrase, Novalins) and brief and manage freelance designers and print partners.
- Packaging: You'll own packaging briefs from start to finish and coordinate agencies (ARD, Superhuit, Carac Design) and freelance packaging designers. You'll keep the work aligned with regulatory, cost and manufacturing constraints.
- Clinical studies: You'll connect the human factors evidence from ClinOps-run trials with the human factors evidence for the product we ship to customers.
- Roadmap and reporting: You'll keep a single human factors roadmap and manage dependencies, resourcing and budgets across teams. Each month you'll report confidence levels and raise any risks to leadership.

This is a part time contractor role of up to three days per week, with a total fee of CHF 17,500 for the initial engagement. We would like to start as soon as possible, with a review after three months. 

Requirements 

What you'll bring 

- Human factors or usability engineering experience in medical devices, ideally with wearables or connected health
- Proven project or programme management: you've owned the plan, sequenced multiple workstreams and delivered on deadlines through others
- Hands-on knowledge of IEC 62366 usability engineering, use-related risk documentation (e.g. UFMEAs) and IFU development
- Experience managing agencies, labs and freelancers
- Clear, confident communication, with a track record of connecting Product, Clinical and Quality/Regulatory teams

First priorities 

- Audit of our current processes and human factors function
- Set up the usability study calendar
- Get a decision on the content split for the QSG "5-minute sheet" redesign

Nice to have: FDA submission experience, a UX research background, and familiarity with InDesign/Figma localisation workflows

Benefits 

At Hilo by Aktiia, our values guide everything we do: 

Move the Needle — You focus on what drives real impact. You let data and clarity guide your decisions, and you take accountability for results. You're a difference maker — you drive ideas to commercial success from start to end. 

Move Fast, Learn, Refine — You work with urgency and purpose, balancing speed with quality. You treat feedback as a chance to learn, and you're deep in customer and partner feedback — translating it to action quickly. 

Team First — You collaborate effectively across teams and build trust through clarity and respect. You're comfortable bridging local execution with a global team, and you communicate openly across time zones.
