title: LNG Commodity Owner
description:
We Are Sparta 

Sparta is the AI leader for commodity trading, home to Leonidas AI, the first operating system for oil and commodity traders.

Backed by $42 million in Series B funding led by One Peak, with participation from returning investors FirstMark and Singular, the same investors behind AI leaders like Legora, Dataiku, and Synthesia. Most companies are building a chatbot on top of data. We've built an agent with an actual reasoning layer, grounded in years of proprietary market data and in-house trading expertise nobody else has.

We're scaling fast, and it's an exciting time to join. From independents to multinationals, the world's leading commodity teams use Sparta and Leonidas AI to move faster, trade smarter, and stay ahead of the market.

At Sparta, you'll be trusted to take ownership, backed by a team who wants you to succeed. AI is how we build here, not just what we sell. Good ideas move fast, and yours could go from staging to production in a couple of hours, whatever department you're in. You'll be challenged, supported, and given room to grow, building the AI that's changing how commodity trading gets done.

Your work has reach. From shaping Leonidas AI, to powering smarter decisions for traders around the world, to changing how commodity trading is done. And because we're growing fast, you'll accelerate your career with a level of ownership and impact you simply won't get at bigger, slower-moving companies.

LNG Commodity Owner, Sparta Commodities 

Singapore, Geneva or London 

LNG moves on netbacks, shipping and a handful of hubs that rarely agree with each other. Plenty of people write about that. We want the person who builds the system that connects all the pieces of the puzzle, and then puts it in front of traders and makes it sell.

Sparta is building the data platform that energy traders, analysts and commercial teams use to make faster, better decisions. We cover forward curves, price assessments, market intelligence and trade flows across the global energy complex. LNG is our next vertical, and we want an exceptional builder to lead it.

The role 

This is a builder's seat. It isn't just an analyst position, a sales role or a thought-leadership seat. You will be leading the development of Sparta's LNG offering, from the first netback model to the AI analyst that puts together a forward view on LNG markets autonomously, working with our engineering, product, data and commercial teams. You will set the direction and stay hands-on: prototyping, testing and shipping with the team, not handing over a spec and waiting. Building on its own is not enough. The job is to build a product LNG desks will pay for, which means time with clients is as much a part of the role as time in the code.

We are looking for someone who knows LNG deeply: JKM, TTF and Henry Hub relationships, netbacks and delivered economics, shipping and regasification costs, cargo arbitrage between basins and contract structures. Your job is to turn that knowledge into products. Expect a good part of your week to be hands-on with AI coding tools: prototyping a pricing model in Python, standing up a data pipeline, creating market-leading knowledge graphs that an AI agent follows and testing its answers against desk judgement. The rest goes on working with engineers to harden, scale and ship what the team builds.

The role reports to our Head of Commodities.

What you'll do 

Building products, data pipelines and AI agents (~55% of role) 

- Lead the design and build of Sparta's LNG product set: netbacks, arbitrage routes, delivered price curves and the analytical tools that sit on top of them

- Build the LNG expert inside Leonidas with our AI engineers: the tools it calls, the domain rules it follows and the knowledge base behind them

- Build automated products with the team: a daily LNG brief autonomously written by AI analyst, alerts on the curves and spreads that matter, and the quality checks that catch errors before clients see them

- Build evaluation sets that test the AI against desk judgement, and keep them passing as the product changes

- Build the data pipelines behind the vertical with data and engineering colleagues: price inputs, freight and regas assumptions, vessel and terminal data, route onboarding and automated data quality checks

- Ship to production with engineering through our normal process (pull requests, code review, tests, CI), and hold the bar on scale, security and reliability

Owning the LNG vertical (~25% of role) 

- Own the LNG vertical end to end: what we build, how well it works and how it performs commercially

- Set and sequence the LNG roadmap with product and technology, so clients get something useful early and more every few weeks

- Write the rules: the LNG conventions, definitions and desk judgement that every Sparta product and agent follows

- Lead the people working on LNG across product, engineering and data: set priorities, unblock them and raise the bar on quality

- Be the person the business comes to for any LNG decision

Building a product clients pay for (~20% of role) 

- Lead discovery conversations and technical demos with LNG trading desks, analysts and commercial teams, and use what they tell you to decide what to build next

- Work with sales and account management on the first LNG deals and on adding LNG to existing oil and freight accounts: you bring the market credibility and the product, sales runs the commercial process

- Give sales a clear account of what the product does and why a desk would pay for it, so they can sell it without you in the room

- Represent Sparta at industry events, conferences and client visits as the LNG expert

What we're looking for 

Required 

- Deep LNG market expertise: strong working knowledge of global LNG pricing (JKM, TTF, Henry Hub and the relationships between them), netbacks and delivered economics, shipping and regasification costs, cargo arbitrage between basins and contract structures

- A track record of building, not just specifying: tools, models, pipelines or products you built hands-on and that other people rely on

- Strong Python and SQL, and comfort with the rest of a modern stack: APIs, databases, cloud services and version control

- Heavy, daily use of AI coding tools to prototype and ship far faster than a traditional build cycle, and the judgement to spot where an LLM gets the market wrong

- Ownership and drive: you scope the problem, pull in the right people, get it built and shipped, and fix it when it breaks, without waiting for a detailed spec

- Credible in front of trading desks: able to run a discovery call and a technical demo, and to hear what a client will pay for and what they won't

- Experience leading or working closely with engineers, and the technical credibility to set direction with them

- Experience in a commodity-facing role within energy trading, data/analytics, financial services or a closely related field

- Ability to turn market complexity into rules, tests and code that make an AI agent answer like a good desk analyst

Desirable 

- Experience building AI agents or LLM applications: tool calling, prompt design, retrieval and evaluation

- Experience shipping work to production alongside an engineering team (code review, testing, CI/CD)

- Familiarity with LNG data sources: price assessments, vessel tracking and shipping data, terminal and regasification data

- Experience with pricing, data or analytics platforms in the energy space, or with building one from scratch

- An existing network within the LNG trading community

What success looks like 

In your first six months, you will have:

- Led the build and launch of the first version of Sparta's LNG offering: netbacks, arbitrage routes and delivered price curves in clients' hands

- Built, with the AI team, an LNG expert in Leonidas that answers the way a good desk analyst would, with an evaluation set that proves it

- Launched at least one automated product, such as a daily brief or a set of alerts, that runs every day

- Written the LNG rules every Sparta product and agent follows

- Set up, with data and engineering, pipelines that run and check themselves, so the vertical scales without manual work

- Put the product in front of LNG desks, helped sales land the first LNG clients, and fed what the market told you back into the roadmap

Is this you? 

This role is for you if you'd rather build the tool than write the note about it, you like being hands-on, you make the people around you build faster too, and you measure what you've built by whether a desk will pay for it. It probably isn't for you if the part of the job you enjoy most is publishing your market view, or you'd rather hand over a spec than help build what's in it.

Why Join Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture is built on innovation, collaboration, and high performance. We thrive in a fast-paced environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are embraced, and impact is rewarded.

• Equity in a high-growth, VC-backed company

• $42M in Series B funding — strong market traction and investment

• Early-stage growth — build your career as we scale

• Market-leading product — we are redefining commodity trading intelligence

• Top-tier tools and technology to support your success

What's the Culture Like at Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture isn't just a set of values on a wall — it's how we work. We embrace a dynamic environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are met head-on, and innovation thrives. You'll collaborate with people who are passionate about our mission and committed to building outstanding products and outcomes for our customers.

The Sparta Code

Understanding is non-negotiable 

Understanding leads to believing. Believing leads to winning. 

The 'why' is the difference between compliance and conviction. Before we execute, we ask: why does this matter, who does it serve, what changes if we win? People who understand the mission don't need to be managed.

Ask for forgiveness, not for permission 

Most decisions are reversible. Most fears are not. 

90% of decisions are reversible. Make them, ship, iterate. Perfection is the enemy of efficiency. Bias for action means moving before you have all the answers, but it isn't recklessness. The rule: tell the rest of us what you did, what changed, what you learned.

Fall in love with the problem 

The mission wins. Your idea doesn't have to. 

Solutions flatter our ego. They feel like progress. But solutions without problems are opinions, and opinions don't move customers, markets, or teammates. The goal is to find what's true, not to win the room. If your idea gets killed because a better one comes along, that's the system working.

It's your fault. Lucky you. 

If it's on you, it's in your control. 

True ownership sounds harsh until you feel how liberating it is. If every problem is yours, you stop spending energy on who to blame and start spending it on how to fix it. Effective leaders default to 'it's on me'. Not out of guilt, but out of agency.

Conflict is a gift 

Honesty is an expression of care. 

Withholding feedback is choosing comfort over growth, yours and your colleague's. Staying silent deprives others of the chance to learn. We challenge openly and with positive intent. Done with care, this builds trust. Done with ego, it destroys it.

We're developing a platform that enables engineering teams to build and run AI-powered software factories, where coding agents take on real development work, from picking up engineering tickets to implementing changes and creating pull requests.

By combining structured context, reusable agent skills, automated workflows and evaluations, we're making AI-powered development more reliable, repeatable and scalable, while keeping humans in control. We're tackling some of the biggest challenges in autonomous software development, from code quality and security to helping organisations confidently adopt AI agents at scale.

Founded by Guy Podjarny, previously founder of Snyk, Tessl is a fast-growing Series A startup backed by over $100 million in funding from investors including Index Ventures, Accel, GV and Boldstart.

Joining Tessl means helping define an entirely new category of technology, solving ambitious technical challenges and shaping the future of software development.

ABOUT THE ROLE 

We’re hiring a Demand Generation Manager to build and scale Tessl’s growth engine.

You’ll own pipeline creation across channels — from experimentation to execution. This is a hands-on, data-driven individual contributor role focused on building repeatable, measurable demand in a developer-first market.

You’ll work closely with Product Marketing, Content, and Sales to ensure we’re attracting the right audiences and converting attention into high-quality pipeline.

If you love testing hypotheses, building systems from scratch, and turning signal into scalable growth, this role is for you..

WHAT YOU'LL DO 

Pipeline Strategy & Execution 

- Own demand generation strategy across paid, organic, partnerships, and community channels

- Build and optimise multi-channel campaigns aligned to product launches and GTM priorities

- Drive MQL → SQL pipeline growth with clear attribution and reporting

Experimentation & Optimisation 

- Run rapid growth experiments across paid media, landing pages, email, and content distribution

- Manage budget allocation across channels based on performance

- Improve conversion rates across the funnel

Performance & Analytics 

- Define and track core growth metrics (CAC, CPL, conversion rates, pipeline contribution)

- Build dashboards and reporting frameworks

- Use data to continuously refine strategy

Cross-Functional Collaboration 

- Partner with Product Marketing on launch amplification

- Align with Sales on ICP targeting and pipeline quality

- Work with Content to maximise distribution and reach

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR 

Must have: 

- 4–8+ years in demand generation or growth marketing (B2B SaaS preferred)

- Experience owning paid acquisition and multi-channel campaigns

- Strong analytical skills and comfort with attribution models

- Demonstrated success building pipeline in early-stage or high-growth environments

- Bias for action and experimentation mindset

Nice to have: 

- Experience marketing to developers or technical audiences

- Familiarity with PLG + sales-assisted hybrid funnels

- Experience with marketing automation and CRM tooling (e.g. HubSpot, Salesforce)

Application Process 

- Introductory call

- Hiring manager interview

- Practical growth case discussion

- Cross-functional interviews

- Final conversation with leadership

Life at Tessl 

We want Tessl to be a place where you can do meaningful work, keep learning and enjoy being part of the team. Alongside competitive compensation, we offer benefits designed to support you both inside and outside work.

What we offer 

- Competitive compensation and equity: Market-benchmarked salaries and EMI share options.

- Time off: 25 days of annual leave, plus UK public holidays, and two paid volunteering days each year.

- Private healthcare: Vitality medical insurance, including dental, optical and mental health support, with cover included for partners and dependants.

- Pension: A 5% employer pension matched contribution through Smart Pension.

- Life assurance: Company-paid life insurance with MetLife providing cover of four times your annual salary.

- Family Leave: We offer enhanced Maternity, Parental and Adoption Leave from day one to support you and your growing family.

- Learning and development: We support opportunities to continue developing your skills with a £1,000 per year to spend.

- Commuting benefits: Financial support for eligible team members commuting from outside Greater London, plus a Cycle to Work scheme.

- Summer & winter offsites: Twice a year, we bring the whole Tessl team together for a week-long offsite. It's a chance to step away from our usual routines, collaborate on big ideas, build stronger relationships and enjoy shared experiences together. And of course, we have a lot of fun along the way!

Our London HQ 

Our office is in the heart of King's Cross, surrounded by London's growing AI and technology community.

We work together in person on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays, giving us time to collaborate, exchange ideas and build relationships. You'll also enjoy catered lunches (Tuesday & Thursday), plenty of office snacks, regular team lunches and socials, plus a pet-friendly workplace.

How we work 

Our operating principles shape how we collaborate and make decisions. We move quickly and learn by doing, build on ideas before challenging them, get stuck in wherever we can help, and give people real ownership. We encourage thoughtful debate, curiosity and a willingness to try things that haven't been done before. Read our five operating principles .

We're AI native 

AI isn't just what we're building - it's central to how we work every day, across every function. We actively use AI to improve how we work, solve problems and challenge traditional ways of doing things.

You don't need to be an AI expert to thrive at Tessl, but you do need curiosity, an appetite for experimentation and a willingness to embrace new ways of working. We expect everyone to use AI regularly, invest time in learning how to get the most from it and keep experimenting when something doesn't work the first time, rather than defaulting to manual approaches.

We're also big believers in sharing what we learn. We encourage transparency about how we're using AI, what's working, what isn't and how we can help each other improve. Being AI native doesn't mean removing human judgement, it means using AI thoughtfully, while taking ownership of the quality and outcomes of our work.

Everyone is welcome at Tessl 

We're committed to building an inclusive environment where people from different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives can thrive.

We particularly welcome applications from people who are underrepresented in technology. If you're excited about the opportunity but don't meet every requirement, we'd still encourage you to apply.

If you need any adjustments or additional support during the recruitment process, please let us know. We're happy to work with you to make the process accessible and comfortable.

Come build with us 

We're moving fast, experimenting boldly and figuring things out as we go. There's plenty to build, lots to learn and real opportunities to make your mark.

If you're excited by big ideas, enjoy getting stuck in and want to be part of something from the ground up, we'd love to hear from you!

We are genuinely multi-cloud, and we are looking for a Senior Cloud Engineer who is too - a strong generalist who treats infrastructure as a software problem and can deliver from week one.

This is a hands-on senior role in an established, fast-moving team. Everything we run is defined in code, deployed through pipelines, and reviewed like software. You will bring deep cloud expertise across AWS and Azure and pair it with a genuine software engineering mindset: you write Terraform modules others build on, you automate away toil rather than documenting it, and you treat the platform as a product with users, SLOs, and a roadmap.

Deep AWS expertise: Advanced, hands-on experience designing and operating production infrastructure in AWS at enterprise scale: multi-account architectures (Control Tower, Organizations, SCPs), IAM, KMS, and the core compute, storage, and security services that a large regulated estate runs on. You should have a proven track record of delivering resilient, multi-region architectures.

Azure experience: Real production experience with Azure alongside AWS: landing zones, VNet architectures, Entra ID, and the Azure resource and governance model. You understand where the two clouds differ and can design well for both rather than forcing one cloud's patterns onto the other.

Software engineering mindset: You treat infrastructure as software. Expert-level Terraform: reusable modules, secure state management, and disciplined code review. Kubernetes: Solid experience running containerised workloads in production, ideally on EKS/AKS: cluster lifecycle, workload deployment patterns, and the operational realities of keeping Kubernetes healthy at scale.

Security and compliance awareness: Experience operating in regulated environments. You understand why change control, least privilege, and auditability matter, and you design controls in rather than bolting them on. Familiarity with PCI DSS is a strong plus.

Engineering excellence: A focus on observability and measurement: you instrument what you build and answer operational questions with data rather than opinion.

Leadership and mentorship: A natural ability to guide and mentor peers, translate ambiguous problem definitions into actionable technical plans, and raise the bar through your code and your reviews.

Pragmatic problem solver: You understand when to move fast (creating tech debt) and when to move right (paying it off). You are a cornerstone in incident resolution and root-cause analysis.

Experience: 5+ years in cloud engineering roles with significant AWS depth. We need someone who can hit the ground running: comfortable joining a complex, established estate and delivering meaningful work in their first weeks, not their first quarter. title: Post-doctorante ou Post-doctorant en transmission et détection sur fibres à cœurs creux - CDD de 18 mois
description:
Qui sommes-nous ? 

Télécom Paris, école de l’IMT (Institut Mines-Télécom) et membre fondateur de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris, est une grande école du top 6 des écoles d’ingénieurs généralistes françaises.

La Raison d’Être de Télécom Paris est de former, imaginer et entreprendre pour concevoir des modèles, des technologies et des solutions numériques au service d’une société et d’une économie respectueuses de l’humain et de son environnement.

Nous recherchons une Post-doctorante ou un Post-doctorant en transmission et détection sur fibres à cœurs creux pour rejoindre le département COMELEC à Télécom Paris.

Les fibres à cristaux photoniques à cœur creux (Hollow-Core Photonic Crystal Fibers, HCPCF) ont récemment franchi une étape technologique majeure, avec des pertes de propagation pouvant atteindre 0.1 dB/km à 1550 nm, comparables, voire inférieures, à celles des fibres télécoms standards [1–2]. La lumière se propageant principalement dans l’air, les HCPCF présentent une latence réduite de 30 à 40 %, une dispersion ultra-faible et des non-linéarités optiques négligeables. Ces propriétés uniques en font des technologies particulièrement prometteuses pour les systèmes de télécommunications de nouvelle génération, la distribution quantique de clés (Quantum Key Distribution, QKD) sur longue distance et les applications de détection distribuée.

Le projet proposé vise à développer et démontrer la prochaine génération de fibres à cristaux photoniques à cœur creux (HCPCF) pour la transmission de données à haut débit et les applications de détection. La propagation de la lumière dans l’air plutôt que dans le verre permet aux HCPCF d’offrir une latence réduite et des non-linéarités optiques négligeables par rapport aux fibres de silice, répondant ainsi à certains des enjeux majeurs des futurs centres de données et réseaux optiques. Notre ambition est de démontrer une transmission à 400 Gbit/s sur quelques kilomètres à travers des échantillons de fibres issus de nouvelles architectures, et d’étudier le potentiel de ces HCPCF pour des applications de détection. La réalisation de ces objectifs nécessite de répondre à des spécifications exigeantes en matière de guidage monomode, de contrôle de la polarisation, ainsi que de faibles pertes par courbure et par couplage.

Deux équipes complémentaires assureront conjointement l'encadrement de ces travaux : le GPPMM, reconnu internationalement pour ses activités de conception et de fabrication de HCPCF [3–5], et le GTO, leader dans la démonstration de systèmes de communication optique et de détection à haut débit [6–8]. Un processus itératif entre la fabrication des fibres et leur caractérisation au niveau système permettra de s'assurer que leurs propriétés répondent aux exigences opérationnelles en matière de transmission et de détection. Sur le plan méthodologique, le projet combinera modélisation numérique, caractérisation et validation expérimentale dans la bande C. Les méthodes de modélisation et de traitement du signal développées au GTO pour le suivi de la polarisation contribueront à évaluer et à optimiser les performances de transmission des HCPCF conçues et caractérisées au GPPMM.

À propos du projet PLEIADES 

Le projet PLEIADES s'inscrit dans le cadre du programme PEPR « Réseaux du futur », financé par l'ANR, et réunit un consortium de 14 partenaires. L'un des axes de travail porte sur les fibres à cœur creux de nouvelle génération et rassemble plusieurs laboratoires académiques, notamment LTCI, XLIM et PHLAM.

Vos principales missions seront de :

- Assurer des missions de recherche dans le domaine de la photonique

- Assurer des missions d’encadrement et de tutorat

- Participer à la notoriété de l’Ecole, de l’Institut Mines-Télécom et de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris

Vous êtes titulaire d’un doctorat ou équivalent en génie électrique, communications, photonique, traitement du signal ou dans un domaine connexe. Vous disposez de solides connaissances en systèmes et réseaux de transmission optique ainsi qu’en traitement numérique du signal (DSP) appliqué aux systèmes de communication ou aux capteurs à fibre optique. La maîtrise de MATLAB et/ou Python pour le développement d’algorithmes DSP sera appréciée. Vous manifestez un intérêt marqué pour la recherche appliquée et êtes à l’aise dans un environnement multiculturel, notamment pour encadrer des stagiaires et/ou des étudiants. Une bonne maîtrise de l’anglais est indispensable. Vous disposez également de bonnes qualités relationnelles et pédagogiques, d’un bon esprit d’équipe et d’une capacité à synthétiser et à communiquer des informations complexes.

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ? 

Vous travaillerez dans un environnement en plein développement, agréable, verdoyant et accessible (notamment pour les personnes en situation de handicap) à seulement 20 km de Paris (RER B et C, proximité des grands axes routiers).

- flexibilité des horaires de travail (en fonction de l'activité du service)

- télétravail 1 à 3 jours/semaine possible

- Remboursement abonnement transports en commun à 75%

- Proximité de nombreuses infrastructures sportives, conciergerie, parking souterrain, restauration interne...

- A savoir : nos cotisations sociales sont moins élevées que dans le secteur privé

title: Head of AI - NLP Healthtech
description:
Chez Lifen, nous pensons que les données médicales ont le potentiel de transformer le système de santé. Mais seulement si elles sont accessibles. Plus de données accessibles → moins de charge administrative, une meilleure coordination des soins et des découvertes scientifiques plus rapides.

Depuis 2015, notre mission est de libérer ce potentiel. Nos solutions basées sur l'IA permettent aux professionnels de santé de partager les informations médicales sans effort et aux chercheurs d'accélérer les découvertes cliniques : avec un impact sur des millions de patients en France chaque jour. Alors que nous nous préparons à nous développer en Europe, 2 choses déterminent notre succès : nos équipes et notre mission.

Aujourd'hui, plus de 150 personnes travaillent depuis nos bureaux et à distance pour libérer le potentiel des données de santé. Nous avons connecté 800 hôpitaux et 150 000 professionnels de santé, et nous ne faisons que commencer. Nous recherchons des personnes qui embrassent la complexité, veulent résoudre des problèmes difficiles et sont prêtes à construire le futur de la collaboration en santé.

⚡ Notre équipe AI 

La santé est un monde de données complexe, fragmenté et hétérogène. L’IA représente une formidable opportunité de dépasser cette limite structurelle, qui freine l’innovation, l’efficience opérationnelle des hôpitaux et les diagnostics médicaux. Avec les algorithmes d’IA de Lifen, la donnée médicale circule mieux, les soignants consacrent moins de temps aux tâches administratives, les parcours de soins gagnent en fluidité et la recherche clinique peut avancer plus vite.

Notre équipe AI travaille à la fois sur des produits qui facilitent la prise en charge des patients au quotidien et sur des projets qui permettent de structurer des données de santé à grande échelle pour accélérer la recherche. Cela veut dire entraîner et faire évoluer nos propres modèles, notamment autour du traitement du langage et des grands modèles de langage, sur des données complexes, hétérogènes et sensibles.

L’équipe réunit des machine learning engineers autonomes et exigeants. Elle a déjà construit des fondations solides. Le prochain cap est clair : donner une direction commune aux sujets liés aux soins et à la recherche, faire des choix ambitieux et transformer des avancées techniques en produits utiles.

Nous cherchons un·e Head of AI capable de tenir ce rôle de chef d’orchestre : proche des enjeux techniques ; à l’aise avec le produit et le business ; capable de faire grandir une équipe.

Le poste est basé à Paris, avec un fonctionnement hybride et une présence régulière attendue aux côtés de l’équipe.

🎯 Ce que tu feras chez nous 

- Définir une stratégie AI lisible et ambitieuse : clarifier les priorités, construire une roadmap, arbitrer entre développement interne, partenariats et solutions existantes, puis donner un cap cohérent aux initiatives liées aux soins comme à la recherche clinique.

- Faire émerger des produits utiles à partir de sujets techniques complexes : par exemple, améliorer la structuration de documents médicaux pour réduire la charge des équipes de soins, ou rendre des données cliniques exploitables pour faire progresser la recherche.

- Orchestrer les priorités d’une équipe très transverse : les besoins viennent de plusieurs produits, avec des horizons et des contraintes différents. Tu apporteras le point de vue AI nécessaire pour choisir où investir, ce qui doit être amélioré et ce qui mérite d’être exploré.

- Faire grandir l’équipe et ses référents techniques : installer des objectifs clairs, du feedback utile et des espaces de décision réels, afin que chacun puisse prendre de l’ampleur sans perdre la qualité d’exécution qui fait la force de l’équipe.

- Garder l’équipe connectée aux évolutions du domaine : challenger les approches établies, lancer des POC, faire évoluer les pratiques et décider avec pragmatisme quand une nouvelle technologie mérite d’être adoptée.

- Porter la vision AI de Lifen auprès des équipes Produit, Tech et de la direction, mais aussi auprès de clients, partenaires et de l’écosystème.

⭐️ Ce que nous recherchons 

Must-have 

- Tu as déjà défini et mis en mouvement une stratégie AI, machine learning dans une entreprise technologique, une scale-up ou un environnement comparable.

- Tu as au moins deux ans d’expérience de management direct d’une équipe Data, AI, Machine Learning ou Engineering.

- Tu as une expérience sur le traitement automatique du langage, les grands modèles de langage, l’extraction d’information ou la structuration de données homogènes qui te donne une une crédibilité technique solide auprès de l’équipe.

- Tu relies naturellement les choix technologiques aux usages, aux utilisateurs et aux résultats attendus pour le produit et l’entreprise.

- Tu sais embarquer des interlocuteurs techniques comme non techniques.

Nice-to-have 

- Tu as déjà travaillé dans la santé, les données cliniques, la medtech, la biotech ou un secteur soumis à de fortes contraintes réglementaires.

- Tu as collaboré avec des équipes de recherche appliquée, publié, contribué à des conférences ou porté des prises de parole sur des sujets AI.

- Tu as évolué dans une organisation où les données sont sensibles et où les enjeux de souveraineté, de confidentialité et de conformité font partie des décisions techniques.

Soft skills 

Tu aimes les problèmes qui ne se résolvent pas avec une recette toute faite. Tu es à l’aise dans l’ambiguïté, curieux·se par nature et assez exigeant·e pour remettre en question les habitudes quand elles ne servent plus l’objectif. Tu sais manager des personnes senior : leur donner du cadre, de la reconnaissance et de l’autonomie.

Nos valeurs 

- Embrace Complexity : tu sais composer avec des données imparfaites, des contraintes réglementaires fortes et des arbitrages techniques qui changent vite.

- Bienveillance : tu crées un environnement de confiance, où l’exigence va de pair avec l’écoute, le feedback et le droit de questionner.

- Real Impact : tu gardes en tête ce que chaque décision peut changer pour les soignants, les chercheurs et, au bout de la chaîne, les patients.

👥 Process de recrutement 

- Échange de préqualification avec Laura, Talent Acquisition Manager, 30 minutes .
Nous faisons connaissance, revenons sur ton parcours, tes attentes et les grandes lignes du poste. C’est aussi le moment de répondre à tes premières questions sur Lifen, l’équipe et le contexte.

- Entretien avec Alexandre, CTO, environ 45 minutes 
Nous approfondissons ton expérience de management, ta capacité à construire une stratégie AI et ta manière de faire le lien entre technologie, produit et enjeux business.

- Étude de cas et échanges avec l’équipe AI, environ 1 h 30 
En amont, nous te partagerons un cadre de réflexion. Tu présenteras ensuite ton approche à plusieurs membres de l’équipe, lors de deux échanges. L’objectif n’est pas de tester ta connaissance d’une stack précise, mais de comprendre comment tu structures une vision, priorises dans un contexte complexe et crées l’adhésion.

- Entretien final avec la direction Tech et Research, environ 1 h à 1 h 30 
Nous échangeons sur ta lecture des enjeux de Lifen, ton ambition pour l’AI appliquée à la santé et ta capacité à porter cette vision au-delà de l’équipe.

Nous nous engageons à te faire un retour dans les 72 heures après chaque étape. Des prises de références pourront être demandées en fin de process, avec ton accord.

title: Senior Talent Partner, Tech
description:
About Dust 

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it. 

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast. 

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50 .

Why this role exists 

We are about to hire the people who will define the next phase of this company. Not backfill a plan someone else wrote — define it. The quality of who joins Dust over the next eighteen months is the single highest-leverage variable in whether we build the category or watch someone else do it.

That work needs a recruiter who treats hiring as a craft rather than a queue. Someone who can hold a real point of view on what "great" looks like for a role, defend it with a hiring manager who disagrees, and then go find that person themselves — from a cold start, without a lead gen team, a sourcing pod, or a playbook waiting for them.

You'll be an early member of a small Talent team. That means you own roles end to end, and you also help build the thing itself: the assessment design, the interview loops, the calibration, the data we use to know whether any of it is working.

We're looking for someone who cares about the candidate experience for all parties internal and external. And prioritizes protecting Dust's culture by being thoughtful, thorough and leading by example in being a true team player.

What you'll own 

Full-cycle hiring, end to end. You run your own searches from role kickoff to close. Sourcing, outreach, screening, interviewing, offer strategy, negotiation. You are the owner of the outcome, not a coordinator of other people's opinions.

Assessment design, not just assessment delivery. For every role you open, you help define what evidence would actually predict success — then you build the loop that surfaces it. You'll push back on interview stages that exist out of habit and replace them with ones that test something real.

Hiring manager partnership with a spine. You'll spend as much time calibrating hiring managers as you do talking to candidates. When a manager says "not quite the right feel," you'll ask what they mean until there's a defensible answer, and you'll say so when there isn't one.

Market intelligence. You'll know your talent market better than anyone else in the building — who's good, where they are, what moves them, what compensation actually looks like right now — and you'll bring that back into how we scope roles and design offers.

The candidate experience. Our hiring process is the first honest sample of what working here feels like. You'll make it expedient, direct, well-communicated, and worth a candidate's time whether or not they get an offer.

Building the function. Process, tooling, structured scorecards, funnel data, quality-of-hire signal. You'll leave the system better than you found it, and you'll be trusted to change it without asking permission first.

Two tracks — tell us which one is yours 

We're hiring for depth in one of two areas. You should have a genuine centre of gravity in one; interest in the other is a bonus, not a requirement.

GTM. Account Executives, Sales Engineers, Customer Success, Marketing, and the leaders above them, across Europe and the US. You know how to assess commercial talent on evidence rather than swagger, and you can tell the difference between a rep who carried a territory and a rep who inherited one.

Technical. Software engineers, infrastructure, product, and design, in a market where the best people are not looking and the second-best are drowning in outreach. You can hold a credible conversation about what someone actually built, and you know why that matters more than where they built it.

How we think about hiring 

We're telling you this up front because if you disagree with it, this will be a frustrating job.

- We don't hire based on pedigree. Logos and school names are weak evidence. What someone has actually done, and what they can demonstrate now, is strong evidence. We design our loops accordingly.

- We hire for evidence, not affinity. "Culture fit" that means "reminds me of me" is how companies get homogeneous and slow. We assess against explicit behaviours tied to how we work, and we write down what we saw.

- Speed and rigour are not in tension. Slow processes are usually a symptom of unclear thinking about the role, not of high standards.

- A no should be as clear as a yes. To the candidate, and internally.

- Some of us came from well-known companies. That's context, not criteria. It isn't why we're here and it won't be why you are. We celebrate everyone's achievements and want to create an environment where diversity of thought and experience of a collective whole makes this place exceptional and lasting.

- Recruiters are operators, not order-takers. If you think a role is wrongly scoped, badly levelled, or shouldn't be open at all, you're expected to say so.

What we're looking for 

- 5+ years in full-cycle recruiting, with meaningful time in-house at a high-growth company. You've hired in an environment with real ambiguity, not just real volume.

- Demonstrable depth in either GTM or technical hiring — you can talk through searches you've run, what made them hard, and what you'd do differently.

- Genuinely strong sourcing. Not "I partner with a sourcing team." You find people yourself, and you write outreach that people reply to because it's obviously written by a human who read something.

- Comfort operating without infrastructure. No playbook, no SDR equivalent, limited tooling to start.

- The judgement and directness to challenge senior stakeholders, and the credibility to be listened to when you do.

- A bias to start. You see the gap and close it before anyone asks you to.

- Excellent written English and a real feel for language. Everything you write is a piece of our employer brand.

- Low ego, high ownership. No job is too big or too small — you'll design an assessment framework in the morning and chase a scheduling conflict in the afternoon.

- Based in Paris, London or New York.

Ideal, but not required: experience hiring in AI or developer-facing companies; experience building or improving a hiring process rather than inheriting one; multi-market hiring across Europe and the US.

You'll be using AI to do this job — properly 

We build the AI operating system that companies use to rewire their work. We expect our own team to be the sharpest possible example of that.

You'll build and run your own Dust agents: market maps, candidate research, interview debrief synthesis, competitive intelligence on where talent is moving. Not as a side project — as how the job gets done. You don't need to have done this before, but you do need to be the kind of person who is genuinely excited to, rather than politely tolerant of it.

You'll also be one of our most credible internal sources of feedback on the product, because you'll be a heavy user of it every day.

Location 

This role is based in Paris, London or New York, and we'd love you to spend real time in the office with the team. A lot of the best things about building at Dust happen because people are in the same room: the energy, the fast decisions, the unexpected conversation that unlocks a hard problem.

We hire people with strong judgement and extend that trust to how they manage their time.

Our process 

We'll tell you the full loop up front, keep it to a small number of stages, and give you a decision quickly. You'll meet the people you'd work with, not a panel of proxies. Expect at least one stage where you work through a real hiring problem with us rather than describing a past one.

If you don't check every box, apply anyway. We're more interested in your potential and how you think than a perfect match to a checklist.

Please send your application and resume in English.

Location 

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust 

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.

If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist. 

Learn how we think and work. 

- Our product constitution, a story about our mission 

- Your Next Co-Worker Isn’t Human , Stanislas Polu , VivaTech 2026. A conversation about AI agents taking on larger parts of work and how teams collaborate with them.

- Dust: Gabriel Hubert on Enterprise AI , Gabriel Hubert , Nasdaq, published May 7, 2026. On Dust’s approach to enterprise AI and building the company in Europe.

description:

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

Marketing Ops is one of Alan's highest-leverage functions. 

It sits at the intersection of marketing strategy, data, and technology — turning systems into growth engines and ensuring every touchpoint with prospects and members is timely, relevant, and scalable.

Alan is growing fast across France, Belgium, Spain, and Canada. But today we're leaving value on the table. On the prospect side , we drive more traffic but can't convert it properly: no scoring, no intelligent routing, no nurturing that adapts to buying intent. On the member side , messaging is one of our primary touchpoints for engagement, retention, and trust — yet nobody operates it strategically. Personalization stays shallow, communication pressure goes unmonitored, and shipping a message often means filing an engineering ticket.

We need Marketing Ops leaders who can architect scalable systems , operate them strategically , and progressively embed AI into workflows — to raise quality, reduce manual execution, and unlock growth without scaling headcount linearly.

⭐️ The Marketing Ops job ⭐️

We are hiring two Marketing Operations Managers , each embedded in a different crew:

- Growth Infrastructure — focused on prospect acquisition: building a unified lead engine that captures, scores, routes, and nurtures across all channels

- Product Platform — focused on member lifecycle messaging: operating Alan's messaging stack as a scalable service across 1.7M+ profiles

Both roles share the same DNA: strong marketing ops fundamentals, data fluency, a product mindset, and the ability to be both hands-on and strategic. Crew placement will be determined based on the candidate's experience, interests, and fit during the hiring process. 

Why is this role interesting? 

- Speed : marketing, product, and sales teams ship campaigns and messages confidently — Marketing Ops turns bottlenecks into force multipliers across every crew

- Trust : clean data, governed attributes, proper segmentation, and enforced rules mean the right person gets the right message at the right time

- Scale : as we grow to millions of members across multiple countries, we need operators who keep our platforms clean and the user experience protected — without scaling headcount linearly

- AI at the frontier : this isn't a maintenance role — you'll identify high-priority use cases for AI agents, train and refine them to a senior marketer's quality bar, and drive real adoption

What will you do with us? 

You'll be a partnership with marketers — not a service desk. You'll partner closely with engineers, data, designers, and cross-functional stakeholders (PMMs, sales, growth, product) within a PM-Tech duo crew model.

Regardless of crew, you will own a core set of capabilities:

- Marketing Automation & CRM : own and optimize our marketing stack ( Customer.io , CRM integrations); build automations that enable marketers to launch campaigns independently, at scale, across all geos

- Data Model & Governance : maintain CRM data quality, attribute/event design, and database hygiene as a sustained practice

- Segmentation & Lifecycle Design : design and maintain lifecycle stages, segmentation logic, routing rules, and re-engagement flows across multiple audiences and geos

- Nurturing Infrastructure : own the nurturing stack and campaign processes; make launches autonomous and compliant

- AI-First Operations : identify, build, and refine AI agents for email copywriting, lead scoring, next-best-action recommendations, and content generation — making marketers AI-powered, not replacing them

- Performance Monitoring : track the full funnel from first touchpoint to conversion; identify leakage and prioritize from data

- Documentation & Enablement : create playbooks, train teams on tools and processes, reduce the marginal cost of new campaigns

Product Platform — you'll operate Customer.io and back-end triggered emails as one governed system, monitor communication pressure and enforce channel rules, define and enforce recipient lifecycle paths, drive 100% Design Studio adoption, and co-own outbound messaging strategy with PMMs and product teams.

- At least one AI agent is in production on a key use case (email nurturing, lead categorization, content generation), with a second scoped or live, and adoption is real

- Any marketer or product Alaner can launch a campaign or ship a message without bottlenecking through ops or engineering

- CRM data model, attributes, and segments are properly owned, documented, and clean — the data we see is data we can act on

- Every contact has a documented path through our messaging — segmentation is sharp, messaging is relevant, and pressure is monitored

- Marketing's contribution to acquisition and engagement is visible and quantifiable, from first touch to conversion

⭐️ Is it you we are looking for? ⭐️

You'll be a great fit for this opportunity if you:

- Have 5+ years in Marketing operations, growth ops, CRM ops, lifecycle marketing, or lead generation in a tech environment (B2B, B2C, or B2B2C)

- Have hands-on experience managing marketing automation platforms at scale ( Customer.io , Braze, Iterable, HubSpot, Marketo, Pardot, Salesforce, or equivalent)

- Have a strong understanding of CRM data models — attribute/event design and data hygiene as a sustained practice

- Can frame and implement processes for lead scoring, nurturing, segmentation, and personalization

- Have a product knack : you can define what's not working, identify what to build next, and see problems as opportunities to bring more value

- Bring data fluency and analytical rigor : you read platform and campaign data, surface anomalies, and draw business insights

- Can be both hands-on and think strategically — you drive the big picture while staying close to execution

- Have strong stakeholder management skills — you'll partner daily with engineering, product, sales, and marketing teams

- Can manage multiple projects simultaneously in a fast-moving environment

- Communicate with excellent written and spoken English 

- Are impact-driven with a strong bias towards improving processes

For this opportunity, we are aiming to hire within the C0-D level range .

Therefore, we offer:

- Flexible vacation policy and flexible working hours . Organize your time as you wish.

- Delightful healthcare insurance: Extremely comprehensive health insurance - 100% for you and your children, 90-100% for partners depending on your country (permanent contracts only). 

- Transport . Generous transit benefit

Every Alaner is paired with a dedicated coach from day one, who helps maximize their impact, nurture engagement, and navigate Alan's values to develop their full potential. Learn more about our coaching culture . 

- Parental leave . Extended parental leave for all new parents, for permanent contracts only.

The Principal Product Manager, Acute Care CT owns the DeepHealth Acute Care CT Suite end to end, with primary accountability for what to build and shared accountability for getting it shipped. DeepHealth is building the Acute Care CT Suite from the ground up to cover detection, care coordination, and reporting for emergency CT, starting with head CT and expanding to chest and abdomen, where minutes saved in stroke, bleeds, and trauma directly affect patient outcomes. The Principal Product Manager, Acute Care CT shapes the suite from day one: owning the roadmap, translating clinical needs into ML and product work, and driving cross-functional delivery on a subset of the suite from data through customer activation. The role does not write code or own technical software design.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Product Strategy and Roadmap

- Own the Acute Care CT Suite roadmap and define what to build, defer, or stop based on evidence.

- Define suite scope across pathology detection modules, software capabilities such as alerting and care coordination, and comprehensive draft reporting.

- Work with emergency radiologists and neuro/stroke teams to distinguish stated requests from real clinical needs, including time-to-treatment, triage, missed findings, and care coordination.

- Translate clinical problems into ML work and set model metrics that reflect clinical value, including sensitivity versus false-positive burden.

- Track the acute care market (including Aidoc, Viz.ai , RapidAI, Nicolab, and peers) and position products with Sales and Marketing.

- Delivery and Cross-Functional Execution

- Own delivery end to end on a subset of the Suite, from data to customer activation, including planning, coordination across data, ML, software, QARA, and Support, tracking, and escalation.

- Run squads for new devices (typically 3 to 9 months), such as ASPECTS detection.

- Coordinate with QARA on the regulatory impact of each release, including EU MDR and FDA 510(k).

- Cut scope or move dates when needed, and escalate further as required.

- Partner with engineering and technical leads without writing code or carrying technical software design.

PLEASE NOTE: This is not an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities and requirements of the position described above. Other functions may be assigned and management retains the right to add or change duties at any time.

Minimum Qualifications, Education and Experience

- Bachelor's degree in a technical, scientific, clinical, business, or related field, or equivalent experience (required).

- 8+ years in product or delivery for medical devices or medical imaging software, with products shipped end to end (required).

- Knowledge of radiology and emergency department workflows (required).

- Knowledge of machine learning in Clinical AI (required).

- Experience running cross-functional delivery across data, ML, software, and QA/RA to fixed dates (required).

- Fluent English (required).

- Hands-on use of AI tools (Claude Code, ChatGPT, or similar) in current work (required).

- Preferred: French language skills.

- Preferred: Acute care, stroke, or emergency imaging background.

- Preferred: Experience with SaMD and regulated environments (EU MDR, FDA 510(k)).

- Quality Standards

- Communicates, cooperates, and consistently functions professionally and harmoniously with all levels of supervision, co-workers, visitors, and vendors.

- Follows all DeepHealth policies and procedures.

- Follows data privacy, compliance, safety and confidentiality standards at all times.

- Practices universal safety precautions.

- Promotes good public relations on the phone and in person.

- Adapts and is willing to learn new tasks, methods, and systems.

title: Backend Engineer - Integration Platform
description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous! 

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains. 

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times. 

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies. 

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America. 

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard. 

About the role 

BLP’s AI agents are only as good as their data: they need reliable context from our customers’ ERP systems, such as SAP, Microsoft Dynamics , or Oracle, and a safe way to write their results back.

We are forming a new backend platform team, and you will be one of its first engineers. You will start by learning our existing data synchronization platform, keeping it reliable, and gradually taking ownership of it. From there, you will build the backend services and tooling that let BLP connect to any ERP system through configuration instead of custom code.

What you'll do 

- Shape the platform: work with the engineers and implementation teams who connect our customers’ ERP systems, find where that work is slow or fragile, and turn it into platform improvements.

- Build great software: design and build clean, maintainable services in Go, and raise the bar through thoughtful code reviews.

- Lead technically: drive technical decisions on key initiatives, influence the product roadmap, and support your teammates as they grow.

- Improve how we work: share what you learn openly and keep improving our processes, tools, and team practices.

title: Head of AI
description:
About Poesis 

Whoever builds the leading intelligence for finance will create far more than returns. Poesis is the AI-native investment firm running autonomous agents that predict markets, construct portfolios, and manage risk. Our founders managed institutional capital at Capital Group ($3T AUM) and led enterprise ML at Goldman Sachs and Amazon. We're building a new type of firm, where live capital is the training ground for an intelligence that compounds with every signal.

About the Role 

Financial markets offer something rare in AI research: a continuous, objective feedback loop where you can test new ideas, measure whether they actually work, and use real-world outcomes to inform what you build next. It’s an opportunity to do frontier research with a direct line between the ideas you explore and their real-world performance. As Head of AI, you’ll lead Poesis’s AI strategy and research, setting the technical direction for how we apply frontier AI to investing. You’ll explore new AI approaches, tackle difficult research problems and help define how we use AI to better understand and predict financial markets. This is a hands-on leadership role where you’ll set the research agenda while continuing to work directly on technical challenges.

Challenges You’ll Work On 

- Set Poesis’s AI research direction, identify the hardest problems worth solving and guide the team's technical work.

- Push the capabilities of foundation models, agentic systems and world models through new architectures and research approaches.

- Explore pre-training, mid-training and post-training methods to improve how models learn, reason and adapt.

- Advance tabular ML research, including emerging methods such as prior-data fitted networks (PFNs).

- Tackle the challenges of learning from small, high-dimensional datasets where traditional ML methods struggle.

- Turn promising research into models and systems that can solve difficult real-world problems.

About You 

- You’ve done exceptional AI research at a frontier AI lab, leading research initiatives and helping set technical direction.

- You have deep expertise in modern AI architectures, model training and machine learning.

- You have a strong research track record, including relevant publications.

- You have strong mathematical and statistical foundations and know how to tackle difficult problems with limited, complex data.

- You’re a hands-on technical leader who can guide other researchers while developing, testing and implementing your own ideas.

Nice to Have 

- Experience with frontier tabular ML methods.

- Experience applying ML to financial markets or complex, high-dimensional datasets.

Location 

Hybrid, 3 days per week on-site at our office in Menlo Park, CA, London, or Zurich. Relocation allowance available.

Compensation 

Competitive cash compensation commensurate with experience, plus equity and carry (share of fund profits). 

Benefits 

We offer excellent medical, dental, and vision coverage, alongside a strong benefits package that includes catered lunches, commuter benefits, and more.

For U.S. candidates, current legal authorization to work in the US required; continuing work visa sponsorship available for full-time employees.

Working at Poesis 

As an early team member, you’ll help shape not just the product, but how the company operates. Your decisions will have lasting impact across the business. You’ll build from first principles, with no legacy systems, or entrenched processes slowing you down. Our team is made up of people from elite companies and universities who are low ego, collaborative, and excited to build together.

title: Abacus Consultant Finance, 80-100 %
description:
Möglichkeit, von unseren Büros in Genf oder Bern aus zu arbeiten. 

Du begeisterst dich für Finanzen und Rechnungswesen, möchtest aber über die Zahlen hinausgehen und aktiv zur Digitalisierung von Unternehmen beitragen?

Bei Fidigit stehen unsere Kunden im Mittelpunkt, denn wir bieten dank der Einführung von Abacus ERP und unseren engagierten Mitarbeitenden einen aussergewöhnlichen Service. Als Teil der Fidinam-Gruppe, eines führenden Beratungsunternehmens in den Bereichen Steuern, Unternehmen, Immobilien und digitale Beratung in der Schweiz, sind wir mit mehr als 15 Standorten weltweit und über 300 Beratern hervorragend aufgestellt.

Mit Standorten in Bern, Genf, Lugano, Luzern und Zürich sind wir der einzige Abacus-Vertriebspartner, der in allen drei Sprachregionen der Schweiz vertreten ist. Wir konzentrieren uns darauf, unsere Kunden in den Bereichen Digitalisierung und Prozessoptimierung zu beraten.

Was du bei uns tun wirst: 

- Du begleitest unsere Kunden bei ihren Abacus-Finanzprojekten, von der Konzeption über die Einführung bis hin zur Schulung.

- Du bist als Berater und Teilprojektleiter tätig und übernimmst die Verantwortung für deinen Fachbereich.

- Du analysierst Finanzprozesse und entwickelst passende Lösungen in Abacus.

- Du arbeitest an Themen wie Finanzflüssen, Kostenrechnung, Anlagebuchhaltung, Budgetierung, Kennzahlen und Reporting.

- Du bist verantwortlich für die Parametrierung der Abacus-Anwendungen in deinem Fachgebiet.

- Du berätst und begleitest unsere Kunden vor Ort oder remote.

- Du baust langfristige Kundenbeziehungen auf und trägst zur kontinuierlichen Weiterentwicklung ihrer Lösungen bei.

Dein Profil: 

- Du verfügst über eine Ausbildung im Finanz- und Rechnungswesen und hast eine hohe Affinität zu IT und Digitalisierung.

- Du beherrschst die Grundsätze des Rechnungswesens und möchtest diese mit ERP-Systemen und digitalen Prozessen verbinden.

- Du verfügst über ausgeprägte analytische Fähigkeiten und arbeitest strukturiert, selbstständig und lösungsorientiert.

- Idealerweise hast du bereits Erfahrung mit der Einführung oder Nutzung eines ERP-Systems in einem KMU-Umfeld. Erfahrung mit Abacus ist ein grosser Vorteil, aber keine Voraussetzung.

- Du schätzt den Kundenkontakt und verstehst es, ihre Bedürfnisse in konkrete Lösungen umzusetzen.

- Du beherrschst Französisch und Deutsch und bewegst dich sicher in einem professionellen englischen Umfeld.

Was wir bieten: 

- Die Möglichkeit, dich bei Fidigit durch Experten im Bereich Finanzen und Abacus-Software weiterzubilden. Zahlreiche Karrieremöglichkeiten in diesem Tätigkeitsbereich in der Schweiz.

- Teilnahme an Schulungen beim Hersteller Abacus in Biel, um dich schnell fundierte Kenntnisse der Abacus-Software anzueignen.

- Abacus Platinum Partner innerhalb einer Unternehmensgruppe mit über 60 Jahren Geschichte.

- Ein motivierendes, dynamisches und vor allem kollegiales Arbeitsumfeld. Ein Team von 8 Mitarbeitenden in Genf, 50 in der gesamten Schweiz. Zusammen mit den Teams von Fidinam sind wir rund 30 Personen an unserem Standort in Genf.

- Flexible Arbeitszeiten und die Möglichkeit, im Homeoffice zu arbeiten.

- Attraktive und marktgerechte Anstellungsbedingungen für alle Kompetenzstufen sowie interessante Zusatzleistungen.

title: Paid Working Student: Medical Device Design and Engineering
description:
About Piomic

Piomic Medical AG is an award-winning Zürich medtech company on a mission to change how chronic and acute wounds are treated. Our lead indication is diabetic foot ulcers, a condition with one of the highest mortality rates in healthcare. Our breakthrough COMS® therapy (Concurrent Optical and Magnetic Stimulation) is a non-invasive treatment that delivers physical stimulation to deep tissue for wound healing. Our team of biologists, engineers and designers combines high-quality medical research with a close focus on the people who use our devices. Our vision: life shouldn't be defined by a medical condition.

What you'll do

- Develop and evaluate concepts for the packaging, fixation and accessories of a medical device
- Design geometry variants in CAD and produce them including additive manufacturing
- Build functional prototypes and demonstrators and test them for handling and fit
- Help develop a test setup that recognizes single-use components, from requirements to a working demonstration

title: Principal Design Engineer - Mechanical Equipment (80-100%)
description:
Lead technically by doing. 

Join our Design Engineering team as a highly experienced individual contributor. You will take on challenging mechanical design problems yourself, from concepts and CAD models to manufacturing drawings, prototypes and tested hardware, while helping the wider team make strong technical decisions. 

As a Principal Design Engineer, you are a hands-on member of our Design Engineering team, designing Climeworks’ CO2 collectors, the heart of our direct air capture plant. Improving how they perform, are manufactured and scale is central to the future success of DAC. 

- Mechanical concept & product design: You personally turn new concepts into robust physical products: developing mechanical concepts, creating CAD models, designing components and complete collector assemblies, producing manufacturing drawings, and supporting hardware through fabrication, assembly and testing. 

- Engineering problem-solving & risk reduction: Your experience helps you find the right solutions faster, anticipate problems early and reduce risk before issues reach manufacturing or testing. 

- CO2 collector design: You take mechanical systems from requirements and concepts through to detailed, manufacturable designs. You develop solutions, perform engineering calculations and make the decisions needed to create robust industrial hardware. 

- First-principles engineering: You use experience and first-principles reasoning to identify risks early, evaluate alternatives quickly and converge on simple, robust solutions. You apply calculations, tolerance analysis, design reviews and testing to reduce uncertainty. 

- Own design from concept to commercialisation: You work directly in SolidWorks to create and modify parts, assemblies and system layouts. You manage complex interfaces, packaging constraints and design changes so the complete system works together. You produce and maintain high-quality 2D manufacturing drawings, including appropriate GD&T, tolerances, materials, finishes and manufacturing requirements. 

- Prototype fabrication, assembly & testing: You stay closely involved after the CAD work is complete. You support prototype fabrication, assembly and testing, investigate issues and incorporate the learning back into the design. 

- Technical leadership & design reviews: You act as a senior technical reference for the team, supporting the Design Engineering line manager with design reviews, engineering standards and approval of critical designs. You support the extended team with technical judgement on complex mechanical design decisions, help maintain strong engineering practices and share your experience through everyday collaboration, mentoring and constructive challenge. 

- Cross-functional engineering collaboration: You work with manufacturing, testing, process engineering, procurement, suppliers and other engineering disciplines to ensure mechanical designs work as part of the complete product. You integrate external design resources where needed. 

What makes you stand out 

Your experience makes your engineering more effective: you spot promising solutions early, expose weak points before they become expensive, and deliver designs that are clear, manufacturable and ready to perform in the real world. 

- Mechanical Design Experience : You bring 15+ years of hands-on mechanical design experience, ideally developing complex industrial equipment from concept through manufacture, assembly and testing. 

- Sheet Metal Design & Manufacturing : You have deep practical experience designing sheet-metal parts, structures and assemblies for manufacture at scale. You understand bending, welding and joining methods, forming, tolerances, material and thickness selection, and how design choices affect tooling, cost, assembly and quality. 

- CAD & Drawings : You are an expert SolidWorks user and remain hands-on with CAD. You personally create high-quality manufacturing drawings and are confident with GD&T and tolerance chains. 

- System Design & Engineering Judgement: You have experience designing from components and mechanisms through subsystems, interfaces and complex assemblies. You understand how decisions at one level affect the complete collector and can balance structures, airflow, movement, sealing, process interfaces, manufacturability, reliability and cost to arrive at robust solutions. 

- Manufacturing & DFMA : You have strong knowledge of machined parts, welded structures, materials and manufacturing processes, and apply DFMA to create robust, cost-effective designs. 

- Collaboration & Technical Leadership : You work effectively with engineers, technicians, manufacturers and suppliers. You share your experience, challenge constructively and help others make better technical decisions. 

- Education:  You have a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or similar.

title: Product Frontend Engineer
description:
quinn is becoming the way people employ, across the globe, through one app. 

quinn is an app-based, managed payroll and employment-administration service. We run it for private households employing a cleaner, nanny, or caretaker, and for businesses that manage employment relationships at scale. The customer stays the legal employer: quinn registers the employment, runs payroll, and handles social insurance, taxes, and filings on their behalf, automated end to end.

Where everyone else sells software, quinn sells the outcome. We don't sell payroll software. We run payroll.

The purpose behind it is simple: Fair employment. For all. Correct and fair employment, made simple and accessible for any employer and any employee, in any market quinn enters. 

Where this is going 

Think about what Revolut did to banking. All of the complexity (the regulation, the clearing, the compliance) handled invisibly in the background, and one simple experience at the front. Nobody using Revolut thinks about what happens behind the screen when they open a new account, swap currencies or send money abroad. It just works, in a couple of taps. Nobody should have to think about it in order to employ someone either.

That is what quinn is building, and it is further along than most people assume: a profitable core business, running today in Switzerland, Germany and the UK, expanding into new markets both by launching and by acquiring. By 2030 quinn intends to be the destination brand for fair employment across six countries and more, on one platform, with one experience.

One platform means one frontend. One experience means it looks and behaves like quinn whether you are in Zurich or in London, a household or a company. In this strategy that is not a nice-to-have. It is the strategy.

Which is why the surface matters more than anything else. Everything quinn does is designed to disappear. The interface is the only part the customer ever sees, and it is the whole proof that the complexity behind it is really handled. 

Why this role exists 

Today , quinn runs on several separate web apps: one per product and market, each with its own frontend, grown over the years as the company grew. Our backend engineers built them alongside everything else, plus an internal admin tool that grew the same way. They all work: thousands of employers run payroll through them every month. But nobody was ever tasked with owning the frontend development, so each one got built the way frontend is built by Backend Developers, seen as a hassle rather than the main aspect users interactive with.

What comes next is one frontend that replaces all of them, built from scratch: one quinn app for employers, employees and our own support team, in the browser first, then in the App Store and Google Play from the same work. Alongside it, the frontend of Maestro, the internal tool that replaces the old admin for batch processes. The phone app is the surface that matters most, so everything is built for it from the first screen rather than adapted to it afterwards.

That is the opening. 

How we work 

We are AI-native, and we mean it operationally rather than as a slogan. AI is how the work gets done here. It is why a small team ships like a large one, and it is a large part of how one person will be able to hold the standard we are describing.

We expect you to be at the front of that. Not to have heard of the tools, to live in them, and to build your own leverage with them: scaffolding, visual regression checks, design-token pipelines, whatever takes manual work out of the way.

And we expect the judgement that has to come with it. AI writes code that looks right and is subtly wrong: structure that doesn't scale, patterns that fall apart three screens later, components that work once and never again. You take the speed and throw away the rest. AI never lowers the bar here. It is the reason the bar can be this high.

Tasks

What you will own 

Everything on the screen:

- The frontend of the quinn app and the web app. App first. One app for everyone who uses quinn: the employer, the employee, and our own support team working inside the customer's account.

- The frontend of Maestro, our internal batch tool. Desktop and dense: queues, runs, tables, filters, multi-select, keyboard shortcuts. A different discipline from the app, built on the same components.

- The component library across quinn Home and quinn Business: one frontend, one experience, every market and every device.

- Whether the app feels native: response, scrolling, gestures, transitions, biometric login, push. Nothing that gives away it isn't native.

- The quality of what you ship. Nothing leaves your hands half-finished.

Where design ends, engineering begins. 

We have a design team, and they own how quinn looks and behaves: the flows, the visual design, the tokens, the component specs. You don't design. You own everything from there: how it is built, and everything a design file cannot reasonably specify, such as gestures, keyboard, safe areas, what happens between the drawn breakpoints, the loading, offline, pending and failed states, what a three-line German label does to a layout that was designed for English. You are in the room before design starts, saying what already exists in the library and what a new pattern costs. Not at the end, receiving a handover. When you and design disagree, they decide how it looks and behaves and you decide how it is built. Nothing enters the component library without both of you.

Requirements

Who we are looking for 

You care about interfaces more than anyone else in the room. You see the two-pixel misalignment without being told, and it bothers you until it is fixed.

You build and maintain UI components and design systems, not one-off screens. You can build a mobile app that feels like one. And you can also build a desktop tool full of tables, filters and keyboard shortcuts, because Maestro is one. You understand UX and how people actually behave, not only how a screen looks. And you write code other people can take over: scalable, structured, documented. Not something that only works while you are in the building.

You are independent and decisive. Nobody will spec every detail for you and nobody will review your pixels.

You are fluent in English, no other language is required. And if you have a portfolio, a live product, or anything you have shipped that you are proud of, show it to us. Not a requirement, but it tells us more than a CV does.

Most importantly: you want this one. Not a frontend role at a company where the frontend is a chore. This one, the app nobody has built yet, the standard nobody has set yet, and a company where getting it right actually decides whether the strategy works.

The Team 

We are a small, fast, direct team. We do not have a lot of process or a lot of hierarchy. We do have a clear strategy, an ambitious plan, and five values we actually mean: Be open, Own it, Speak up, Keep it simple, Bias for action.

This is one of the most important hires we will make this year. We are not rushing it and we are not filling a seat. We are looking for the person who reads this and thinks: finally.
