title: Senior AI Developer, Agentic Systems
description:
Company Description

Workleap is a Montreal-based tech company, founded in 2006. We're builders at heart, we make simple products that actually matter to the people who use them. We have two product lines: Workleap Agent , our newest solution built to make every manager more effective, and ShareGate , the world's leading solution for Microsoft 365 migration and governance. More than 15,000 companies worldwide trust us to do exactly that. We're intentional about who joins us. If you're the kind of person who gets excited by a hard problem and wants to help shape what comes next, there's a place for you here.

Your role

At Workleap, our engineering teams already ships more than twice as fast with AI. Now we’re expanding beyond code to everything around it: briefs, specs, design, launch, and measurement. The idea is simple: agents do the work, and people make the calls. We’ve are rethinking how we build products and are exploring the technical possibilities, this is just the beginning. As a Senior AI Developer, you’ll join us to shape and build this solution ensuring that we have solid technical foundation.

Your impact: 

- Ship the first production agents with our Product Managers, starting with brief creation and the ProductManager-to-design handoff, then extend to the rest of the product lifecycle.

- Shape the shared architecture and standards (orchestration, skills, memory, evals, guardrails) so that both our product lines are built on the same foundation.

- Own the production quality of these agents: observability, testing, security, and cost built in from the start, with human approval at every gate.

- Co-design with Product Managers: understand how they work, reuse what they’ve already automated, and ship small iterations they test and adopt.

- Measure what works: time saved, time from customer signal to shipped decision, and cost per agent and per feature, then cut what doesn’t add value.

- Grow others: share your agent development practices so the team can build, run, and improve agents on their own.

Your team

Over the next 6 to 12 months, you’ll work on questions like: how does an agent turn an idea into a brief that a Product Manager approves without rewriting it? How do specialized agents pass context without losing it or blowing up costs? How do we decide an agent is reliable enough to lighten a gate? The vision is set, and a proof of concept in Slack is underway: you’re joining early enough to shape the architecture and turn this start into a production standard.

You’ll join the Product Ops team , a small team serving Product Manager across two product lines that already owns tracking, product data quality, and analytics. You’ll work daily with this team, our AI-Software Development Life Cycle team, which already automates software delivery, and with our Product Managers working on both product lines. You’ll also partner with the Senior AI Developer on our Data team to share patterns and tooling. We use AI every day, decide fast, and ship in iterations.

Our technology ecosystem includes Claude (Claude Code, skills, Managed Agents, Design), MCP, Slack, Jira, Confluence, GitHub, Mixpanel, Snowflake, Azure, etc .

What you'll bring

- Strong production engineering across the agent development lifecycle;

- Hands-on experience designing and shipping multi-agent systems to production: orchestration, tools, context, and memory, integrated with tools like Slack, Atlassian, and MCP;

- Experience instrumenting and evaluating non-deterministic systems: evals, observability, regression testing, and cost tracking;

- Sound architectural judgment across reliability, security, and cost, including which model fits which job, and the confidence to form and defend a technical opinion;

- Experience building components or tooling that other people adopt;

- Real product sense: you understand how a Product Manager works and you build with users, not for them;

- A taste for building as a team and helping people change how they work, by sharing your practices;

- A builder mindset: you own what you ship, you’re comfortable with the ambiguity of an early-stage project, and you use AI-assisted development tools daily and critically;

- Bonus: product management experience, or experience on a B2B SaaS, HR, or IT product.

Most of this sounds like you? Apply.

The internal title for this role is Senior AI Developer - Product Operations.

What the job comes with

- Base salary: $140,000 - $170,000. This range reflects our Canada-wide compensation scale. Final offers may be adjusted based on the candidate's region to align with local market conditions.

- Annual bonus program.

- LTIP program, share in Workleap's long-term growth.

- RRSP + Family health insurance + telemedicine + annual wellness budget.

- Flexible vacation policy.

- Remote work, with access to our Montreal office.

- In-person gatherings twice a year.

- Claude access, for everyone.

What drives us 

At Workleap, we build software that sits at the center of how people experience work, every day, at every level.

We move fast. Priorities shift, decisions get made with the information we have, and we iterate. If you thrive on intensity and ambiguity doesn't slow you down, you'll feel right at home.
We're builders. We do what it takes to move forward. AI is part of our toolkit. We use it to go faster and decide smarter, not to replace judgment.

If you want real impact and a place where your decisions matter, this is it.

How we hire 

Transparency is how we hire — for you as much as for us.

You'll then complete a take-home case study, followed by a meet with future colleagues to discuss it together. description:
At Jamf , we believe in an open, flexible culture based on respect and trust. Our track record and thriving work environment all stem from the freedom we grant ourselves to get the job done right. We take pride in helping tens of thousands of customers around the globe succeed with Apple.

The secret to our success lies in our connectivity, while operating with a high degree of flexibility. Work-life balance remains our priority while feeling connected is important to maintain our strong culture, achieve our goals, and thrive as #OneJamf.

What you'll do at Jamf 

The Digital Success Engineer builds the automation, tooling, and integrations that power Jamf’s digital customer success motion — the agents, agentic workflows, and connected systems that deliver proactive, one-to-many engagement at scale. Reporting to the Director, Strategic Programs, the role partners with the Digital Success Strategy Manager, who owns the strategy and requirements for the motion, turning that vision into working, maintained technology that reaches customers and drives adoption.

What you can expect to do in this role: 

- Builds and maintains the automation, tooling, and integrations behind the digital customer success motion, including agentic workflows, in-app guidance, and the connectors that tie them to systems such as Snowflake, Salesforce, Gainsight, and Slack.

- Turns the strategy and requirements set by the Digital Success Strategy Manager into working technology including scoping, building, testing, and shipping the components that deliver the engagement model.

- Monitors, troubleshoots, and improves the digital-success tooling in production, including fixing issues, versioning changes, and keeping the motion running reliably.

- Implements the logic that targets and personalizes engagement — translating adoption, health, and usage signals into the triggers and flows that drive proactive outreach.

- Applies AI-assisted and modern development tooling — agent and prompt engineering, version control, and connector-based (MCP) workflows — evaluating outputs for accuracy before they reach customers.

- Builds in the guardrails for automated customer-facing communication — draft-first review, human approval where needed, and controls that keep the motion safe to run at scale — consistent with the governance set for the motion.

- Partners with the Customer Success Analytics Engineer and data teams on the data, definitions, and pipelines the tooling depends on.

- Documents and packages what is built so it can be maintained, reused, and handed off.

- Works with general autonomy on how to build, taking direction from the Digital Success Strategy Manager on what to build and in what priority, and escalating cross-functional or technical decisions as needed.

- Evaluates emerging AI tools, models, and platforms, and recommends adoption where they meaningfully improve the reliability, speed, or reach of the digital customer success motion.

- Other duties and special projects as assigned.

What we are looking for: 

- Minimum of 4 years of experience in a technical build role — software or automation engineering, solutions or integration engineering, analytics engineering, or similar — ideally in a SaaS or customer-facing context (required)

- Hands-on ability to build and maintain automation and integrations — comfort with APIs, data connectors, and scripting or low-code automation across systems such as Snowflake, Salesforce, Gainsight, and Slack (required)

- Experience building against defined requirements and priorities, turning a strategy or specification into working, tested technology (required)

- Familiarity with AI-assisted development — agent or prompt engineering, or connector-based (MCP) workflows — and evaluating AI-generated outputs with critical judgment (preferred)

- Comfort with version control (e.g., git) and modern software and data-stack practices (required)

- Working knowledge of customer success or customer-engagement data and metrics (preferred)

- Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work from direction and partner across strategy, data, and customer success teams (required)

EDUCATION AND CERTIFICATIONS 

- Bachelor’s degree in a technical, quantitative, or related field, or equivalent experience (required)

- A combination of relevant experience and education may be considered.

- Certifications in relevant development, automation, or data platforms (preferred)

title: Senior Backend Engineer (Mobile Monetization) | Feeld
description:
GT was founded in 2019 by a former Apple, Nest, and Google executive. GT’s mission is to connect the world’s best talent with product careers offered by high-growth companies in the UK, USA, Canada, Germany, and the Netherlands.

On behalf of Feeld , GT is looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to help them improve their inclusive dating application.

About the Client 

Founded in 2014 as a dating app, Feeld gathered millions of users in one place to create a safer and more inclusive space online for everyone open to experiencing people and relationships in a new way. Their mission is to elevate the human experience of sexuality and relationships and create a world where everyone is more intimately connected to each other and themselves.

The technology stack of the project: Node.js, NestJS, GraphQL/REST, TypeScript, AWS, DynamoDB, PostgreSQL, SQS, EventBridge, WebSockets.

About the Role 

We are looking for a Senior Backend Engineer (Mobile Monetisation) to take ownership of the backend systems powering Feeld's subscription and in-app purchase experiences across iOS and Android.

The ideal candidate brings strong hands-on experience with mobile monetisation platforms such as Adapty, RevenueCat, or similar solutions , as well as integrating mobile payment flows with custom backend services. This includes managing subscription lifecycles, synchronising payment data, handling receipts, and ensuring accurate entitlement management.

We're looking for a highly experienced, proactive engineer with the potential to act as a technical lead , capable of independently driving complex technical initiatives, contributing to architectural decisions, and ensuring the reliability and scalability of revenue-critical systems.

📌 Full-time, long-term
⌛️ Preferred immediate start

Responsibilities: 

- 
Take ownership of the backend systems supporting Feeld’s monetisation, ensuring their reliability, performance, and contribution to business goals.

- 
Design, develop, and maintain scalable backend services and integrations for subscriptions, billing, payment processing, entitlements, pricing, and promotional features.

- 
Ensure the accuracy, stability, and reliability of monetisation flows, proactively identifying and resolving production issues that could impact revenue or user experience.

- 
Support the development and optimisation of subscription and payment flows, including improvements to system performance, scalability, and error handling.

- 
Implement and maintain feature flags, testing, and analytics instrumentation to support experimentation and continuous improvement of monetisation features.

- 
Collaborate with Product, Engineering, and Data teams to build and improve analytics and reporting capabilities, providing insights into revenue performance, user behaviour, and system health.

Essential knowledge, skills & experience: 

- 
5+ years of commercial backend development experience , ideally building high-load, business-critical systems.

- 
Proven experience with mobile monetisation and subscription platforms , such as Adapty, RevenueCat, or comparable solutions.

- 
Hands-on experience implementing mobile in-app purchases and subscription flows for iOS and/or Android applications, beyond web-based payment integrations.

- 
Experience integrating mobile payment platforms with custom backend systems , including payment data synchronisation, receipt handling, subscription status tracking, and entitlement management.

- 
Strong understanding of mobile subscription and payment lifecycles , including renewals, cancellations, refunds, failed payments, and subscription state changes.

- 
Experience ensuring the accuracy, reliability, and consistency of revenue-critical backend systems , including troubleshooting production issues.

- 
Strong backend development experience with Node.js or TypeScript or JavaScript , ideally using NestJS and building GraphQL or REST APIs.

- 
Good understanding of event-driven architectures, asynchronous processing, and distributed systems .

- 
Experience writing reliable unit and integration tests .

- 
Strong technical ownership, independent problem-solving, and architectural decision-making skills, with the potential to take on technical leadership responsibilities .

- 
Strong communication skills and full professional proficiency in English. 

Nice to Have

- 
Experience with AWS cloud infrastructure , SQL and NoSQL databases. Our current stack includes ECS, DynamoDB, SQS, EventBridge, and PostgreSQL.

- 
Experience working directly with Apple App Store and Google Play billing ecosystems .

- 
Experience running monetisation experiments , including A/B testing, subscription pricing changes, and conversion optimisation.

- 
Experience managing regional pricing, multiple currencies, and country-specific monetisation strategies .

- 
Experience analysing the performance of monetisation experiments, including revenue, subscription conversion, and retention metrics.

- 
Previous experience acting as a Tech Lead or Lead Backend Engineer , mentoring engineers, and driving technical decisions.

Interview Steps 

- 
GT interview with Recruiter

- 
GT technical interview

- 
Client technical interview

- 
Final interview

- 
Reference Check

- 
Offer

title: Product Engineering
description:
Product Engineering at Polar

Product engineering at Polar is about shaping and building the finance layer for the next generation of AI products. We’re rethinking how billing works for a world of usage-based software, programmable pricing and AI agents – from real-time metering and pricing as code, to more flexible customer identities, giving developers greater control over how they monetize their products.

We’re interested in engineers who enjoy working across our entire stack, solving complex technical challenges while shaping how developers interact with and experience Polar. We value engineers who think beyond implementation, challenge assumptions and bring the technical depth and product judgement to make sophisticated systems feel simple.

We operate as a small, remote-first team with a strong bias towards shipping. We value engineers who can work independently, collaborate when it matters and maintain a high bar for quality without sacrificing speed.

More about Polar and how we work 

What you could work on

Depending on your experience and where you can have the greatest impact, this could include:

- 
Own product development end-to-end: Identifying opportunities, shipping and iterating on features across our stack – taking responsibility for both the technical implementation and the product outcome.

- 
Build exceptional developer experiences: Bringing a strong eye for design, usability and detail to everything you ship. Turning complex billing and monetization workflows into intuitive interfaces, powerful APIs and thoughtful abstractions that make our merchants’ lives easier.

- 
Ship with speed and quality: Delivering improvements continuously, balancing fast iterations with robust engineering, performance and attention to detail.

- 
Stay close to our users: Engaging with our merchants, to understand how they use Polar, uncover pain points and translate feedback into meaningful product improvements.

What we look for

We’re particularly interested in senior engineers who combine strong technical foundations with exceptional product judgement and design sensibility. People who care deeply about developer experience, have opinions about what makes great software and know that building the right thing often means knowing what not to build.

Some of the qualities and experience we value in this area include:

- 
Strong technical foundations: Experience building, shipping and evolving production software, with deep expertise in at least one part of the stack and the ability to work confidently across frontend and backend systems. You’ve built and maintained products long enough to understand how early technical and product decisions hold up as they evolve and scale.

- 
Product judgement & design sensibility: A deep appreciation for how products look, feel and work. An understanding that developer experience is the product, from the clarity of an API to the smallest details of an interface. Strong opinions, loosely held, and the judgement to challenge assumptions, simplify complexity and know what to leave out.

- 
Ownership & pragmatic execution: The ability to take problems end-to-end with high ownership and autonomy, navigate ambiguity, make decisions without perfect information and take responsibility for outcomes. A bias towards shipping and knowing when to iterate quickly and when to invest in stronger foundations.

- 
Engineering craft: A commitment to the quality of what gets built – from clean APIs and robust backend logic to thoughtful interactions, edge-case handling and performance. High standards for both technical quality and the experience delivered.

- 
Curiosity & collaboration: A willingness to wear multiple hats, collaborate openly and contribute to a small team. Curiosity to learn new technologies and use tools, including AI-assisted development, while maintaining intimacy with the code, sound engineering judgement and ownership of what gets shipped.

Experience with payments, billing or developer tools is a strong plus.

We also love seeing open-source contributions and side projects.

Our stack

- 
Frontend: Typescript (React, Effect)

- 
Backend: Python (FastAPI, Dramatiq)

- 
Infrastructure: Postgres, Clickhouse, AWS.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Data Product
description:
Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

The Data Product team collaborates with an experienced group of data scientists, engineers, and product managers to build highly scalable features that power TRM's products and services. As a Data Engineer on the Data Product team, you will be responsible for designing and building mission-critical data services. These features analyze and provide insights into blockchain transaction activity at petabyte scale, and ultimately work to build a safer financial system for billions of people..

The impact you’ll have here: 

- 
Build highly scalable features that integrate with dozens of blockchains.

- 
Design and architect intricate data models for optimal storage and retrieval to support sub-second latency for querying blockchain data.

- 
Collaborate across departments, partnering with data scientists, backend engineers, and product managers to design and implement novel data models that enhance TRM’s products.

What we’re looking for: 

- 
Bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science or a related field.

- 
A proven track record, with 5+ years of hands-on experience in architecting scalable API development, distributed system architecture, guiding projects from initial ideation through to successful production deployment.

- 
Exceptional programming skills in Python, as well as adeptness in SQL or SparkSQL.

- 
Versatility that spans the entire spectrum of data engineering in one or more of the following areas:

- 
In-depth experience with data stores such as BigQuery and Postgres.

- 
Proficiency in data pipeline and workflow orchestration tools like Airflow and DBT.

- 
Expertise in data processing technologies and streaming workflows including Dataflow, Spark, Kafka, and Flink.

- 
Competence in deploying and monitoring infrastructure within public cloud platforms, utilizing tools such as Docker, Terraform, Kubernetes, and Datadog.

- 
Proven ability in loading, querying, and transforming extensive datasets

About the Team: 

- 
Our team is spread out over several countries and time zones. To leverage the opportunities and address challenges that come with this working model, we've built a culture grounded in trust, transparency, and adaptability. Even though we're scattered across different time zones, we stay closely connected through open communication and regular check-ins. Our use of digital tools helps us collaborate seamlessly and work at an impressive pace, delivering results at TRM speed while staying in sync.

- 
The diversity of perspectives and expertise within our team sparks creative exchanges and enhances our problem-solving capabilities, allowing us to leverage our global synergy to drive innovation and efficiency.

- 
We're driven by a deep sense of ownership, constant pursuit of improvement and an obsession with delivering magical experiences to our customers; these are a core part of our culture.

- 
We're driven by the desire to continuously hone our craft and to this end, we regularly assess our processes, seek feedback, and embrace iterative development to refine what we do.

- 
We structure problems and use the 80/20 rule(for many outcomes, roughly 80% of consequences come from 20% of causes) to identify where to direct our razor-sharp focus.

- 
Each of us is passionate about excellence and growth, and we're encouraged to challenge the status quo and experiment with new methods. This mindset creates an environment where innovation is part of our daily routine and every team member is an impact-oriented trailblazer.

- 
By celebrating our successes and learning from our setbacks, we stay agile and forward-thinking, always striving to elevate our performance and impact.

Learn about TRM Speed in this position: 

- 
The team received a request from customers to show the running balance for assets tied to an address within the product. They brainstormed to determine the minimal viable solution that could be delivered within two weeks. The team decided to develop a framework that would facilitate enabling this feature for each chain (such as BTC, ETH, etc.) individually. They successfully implemented and tested this solution for the BTC chain and delivered it to customers within the two-week timeframe. This approach allowed the team to quickly provide value to customers and establish a repeatable process.

- 
The team was tasked with implementing a new feature that would enable TRM to gather feedback from the user community swiftly. Due to the company's goal of showcasing the feature at an upcoming event, the timeline was tight. The team quickly adjusted to the request, assessed the requirements, and developed a solution that addressed 80% of the needs and could be executed within a very short timeframe. They successfully delivered the feature on schedule, impressing customers with both the functionality and the speed of execution.

- 
The team was tasked with developing a solution to reveal Indirect Exposure through cross-chain swaps in response to a competitor's similar feature. Before choosing the technical approach, the team consulted with stakeholders to establish a feasible timeline for the implementation. With this input, the team devised a solution that fit the timeline, communicated the tradeoffs to stakeholders, and successfully delivered the solution as promised.

About TRM's Engineering Levels: 

Engineer: Responsible for helping to define project milestones and executing small decisions independently with the appropriate tradeoffs between simplicity, readability, and performance. Provides mentorship to junior engineers, and enhances operational excellence through tech debt reduction and knowledge sharing.

Senior Engineer: Successfully designs and documents system improvements and features for an OKR/project from the ground up. Consistently delivers efficient and reusable systems, optimizes team throughput with appropriate tradeoffs, mentors team members, and enhances cross-team collaboration through documentation and knowledge sharing.

Staff Engineer: Drives scoping and execution of one or more OKRs/projects that impact multiple teams. Partners with stakeholders to set the team vision and technical roadmaps for one or more products. Is a role model and mentor to the entire engineering organization. Ensures system health and quality with operational reviews, testing strategies, and monitoring rigor.

Application Instructions 

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM 

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

- 
Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

- 
Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

- 
First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

- 
Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

- 
References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

- 
Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

- 
Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM 

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

- 
Accelerate repeatable workflows

- 
Structure and solve problems

- 
Improve output quality

- 
Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM 

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

- 
Priorities and targets to change quickly

- 
Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

- 
A high level of personal ownership and accountability

- 
Close collaboration across teams and functions

- 
Frequent, high-touch communication

- 
Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

- 
A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute. 

Leadership Principles 

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

- 
Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

- 
Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

- 
Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission 

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
Forward Deployed Engineer 

Sydney or Melbourne (Hybrid)

About Nash 

Nash is building the digital logistics infrastructure that powers delivery for some of the world’s largest retailers, tech platforms, and delivery services. Our platform connects merchants, carriers, and customers through unified AI-driven logistics, helping enterprises like Walmart, Woolworths, 7-Eleven, and Coles orchestrate millions of deliveries every month.

We’re now expanding our engineering presence in Australia and looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer who can ship code, solve real customer problems, and help shape how Nash scales across APAC.

The Role 

This is hands-on engineering at the edge — not pre-sales, not implementation. You’ll build, deploy, and operate production software directly with customers while working closely with our global product and AI teams.

You’ll be part of the foundational team defining how our Australia engineering office operates. Expect to move fast, own outcomes, and see your work drive real-world impact within weeks, not quarters.

What You’ll Do 

• Build and deploy production systems used by top enterprise retailers

• Work directly with customers’ engineering, ops, and leadership teams

• Take new products from concept to live deployments

• Design and extend core infrastructure underpinning global delivery orchestration

• Partner with product and AI teams to influence direction across APAC

• Debug real-world logistics workflows across fleets, APIs, and integrations

Who You Are 

• 4 plus years building and shipping production software

• Strong experience with APIs, backend systems, or platform integrations

• Comfortable jumping between code, customer problems, and architecture decisions

• Bias toward speed, iteration, and ownership

• Clear communicator who can work directly with operators, CTOs, and execs

• Motivated by building software that touches the physical world at scale

Why This Role 

If you’ve wanted to join a high-velocity YC-backed startup redefining how logistics works worldwide — while getting to build and see your code operate inside real enterprise workflows — this is the one.

Your work will touch millions of deliveries each month and help define Nash’s engineering footprint across APAC.

More about Nash 

Nash is the platform that powers modern logistics. 

Commerce has inverted. For decades, customers came to where products and services were. Now products and services come to them, on their terms, in real time. That shift has turned every company into a logistics company, even though almost none of them were built to be one. Couriers, fleets, gig workers, parcel carriers, in-store labor, and increasingly autonomous systems all have to be coordinated in real time, against tighter windows and rising expectations, with hard-fought customer trust on the line.

Nash unifies decisioning, execution, and capacity into a single programmable platform. Real-time, AI-native intelligence determines what should happen, operational control executes it, and the platform dynamically orchestrates capacity from any source: a company's own fleets, partners, or the Nash delivery network. Whether a job involves a courier, a gig driver, an internal fleet, a store employee, a technician, or an autonomous vehicle, Nash selects the right resource and manages execution through completion.

We power delivery and logistics for some of the most recognizable brands in commerce, including Walmart, Urban Outfitters, 7-Eleven, and Woolworths, alongside platforms like Shopify and Toast. Over the next decade, logistics will become as foundational to commerce as payments, cloud, and connectivity. Nash is the platform that powers it.

Nash was founded in 2021 by Mahmoud Ghulman (2x Founder, MIT) and Aziz Alghunaim (2x Founder, 2x YC, Ex-Palantir, MIT) and is backed by Y Combinator, a16z, and other top investors. We are headquartered in San Francisco.

What You’ll Love About Us 

✅ Early-stage, well-funded startup – directly impact the company and grow your career!
✅ Quarterly broader team on-sites to bond with teammates
✅ Competitive compensation and opportunity for equity
✅ Flexible paid time off
✅ Health, dental, and vision insurance for US employees

title: AI Lead / Engineering Manager
description:
This role is part of our Usersnap team, one of our growing brands at saas.group.

Profile Overview

Usersnap is building AI-driven capabilities into the core of the product, from automated setup to intelligent surveys, contextual analysis, and reporting that generates itself based on connectors. We're looking for a hands-on AI Lead / Engineering Manager to lead the small engineering team that ships these capabilities, and to set the technical direction while doing it.

This is a player-coach role. You'll write and review code, make architecture calls, and define what "good" looks like for AI-native development. You'll also own team coordination, delivery timelines, workload allocation, and follow-through, so that work planned is work shipped, reliably and at production quality.

This is a full-time, engineering-led role. It is not combined with product management: the technical leadership scope is substantial on its own, and you'll partner with Product rather than absorb it.

AI capability is becoming core to Usersnap's product and go-to-market, especially as we move upmarket. You'll be the person who makes sure it ships well.

Your immediate impact in the first 3-6 months will be:

- You'll have established a clear delivery rhythm for the team: shared priorities, realistic timelines, visible workload, and projects that get followed through to launch

- You'll have assessed the current state of the codebase, tooling, and practices, and set out a concrete engineering bar covering observability, testing, security, and architecture

- You'll have shipped at least one AI-powered feature to production with the team, from prototype through launch, using timeboxed AI development

- You'll have built a strong working relationship with Product and the rest of the company, and be seen as a reliable owner of ambiguous, technically complex work

- You'll have raised the team's standards while keeping people motivated and engaged

Your responsibilities

Team leadership and delivery 

- Own team coordination, delivery timelines, workload allocation, and project follow-through for a small engineering team

- Keep work moving: break down ambiguous goals, sequence them with Product, flag slippage early, and make sure commitments are met

- Give clear, constructive technical feedback in code review, design discussions, and 1:1s, and raise standards without demotivating people

- Grow the team's capability, including how we use AI tooling to work faster without lowering quality

Technical leadership

-

Hands-on contribution

What You bring to the table

title: Creative Technologist (contract)
description:
Instrument is a digitally native design and technology company built to help brands unlock their full potential. Since 2005, our team of makers, thinkers, and storytellers has partnered with leading brands like Google, Nike, Uber, ŌURA, and Eventbrite to craft digital experiences that create impact and drive results.

Unlike traditional agencies, we don’t just design—we build. Our work lives at the intersection of taste and technology, powered by curiosity, thoughtful curation, and a commitment to delivering the most fitting solution for every brief. We bring this to life across three core offerings: Brand, Marketing, and Product. 

As a member of our freelance network, you’ll collaborate with our teams to bring bold ideas to life—whether launching new brands, building digital products, or shaping experiences that move people. We welcome collaborators from all backgrounds and experiences who share our curiosity, creativity, and care for craft.

We believe great work comes from diverse perspectives and shared purpose. If you’re passionate about learning, experimenting, and making work that matters, we’d love to hear from you.

The Role

We’re looking for an embedded, hands-on Creative Technologist to rapidly turn emerging AI capabilities into compelling, functional experiences.

Working closely with a multidisciplinary creative team, you’ll experiment with new AI model releases and capabilities, quickly moving from “what could we do with this?” to working prototypes and demos people actually want to engage with. You have your finger on the pulse of what’s happening across AI—following new launches, features, and the creative behaviors gaining traction, and recognizing opportunities to build while the conversation is happening.

This is a highly hands-on role for someone who thrives in experimentation. You’re comfortable with ambiguity, curious about what’s next, and able to independently take an idea from early exploration through something polished enough to put in front of an audience.

Contract: ASAP – February 26, 2027
Commitment: 40 hours/week

What You'll Do

- Stay deeply plugged into new AI launches, features, and emerging creative behaviors, identifying opportunities to build while the conversation is happening.

- Rapidly concept, prototype, and ship AI-powered demos that showcase new model capabilities in timely, culturally relevant ways.

- Turn technical capabilities into social-first demos and experiences that are immediately understandable, compelling, and designed to earn attention.

- Use AI-assisted development, “vibe coding,” and rapid experimentation to move quickly from idea to working experience.

- Experiment beyond the obvious use case, developing creative approaches, workflows, or reusable techniques that help others push a capability further.

- Translate experiments into compelling outputs across formats, including working code, screen recordings, short-form social content, technical tutorials, and open-source repositories.

- Partner closely with creative, design, engineering, and production teams to shape ideas while bringing a strong technical point of view.

- Iterate quickly based on creative and technical feedback, balancing speed with a strong bar for craft and execution.

What You Bring

- Strong hands-on experience in creative technology, prototyping, creative development, or a similar technical discipline.

- A portfolio demonstrating functional prototypes, interactive experiences, experiments, or other technically driven creative work.

- A track record of actively experimenting with new AI models, features, and capabilities as they launch, with recent examples of work that responds to emerging trends or behaviors in the AI landscape.

- Meaningful hands-on experience building with Gemini and Google’s AI developer ecosystem, alongside fluency in the broader generative AI landscape.

- Strong coding and prototyping skills using modern front-end frameworks and development tools.

- Strong instincts for what is gaining traction with developers and creators, why it’s resonating, and how an emerging behavior can translate into a compelling demo or piece of social-first content.

- Comfort experimenting with newly released models and capabilities and figuring things out without an established playbook.

- Strong creative instincts and an understanding of what makes a technical demo surprising, useful, entertaining, or worth sharing.

- The ability to work independently and move quickly from an ambiguous idea to a functional prototype with minimal hand-holding.

- Strong communication skills and the ability to make technical ideas accessible and exciting to both developer and broader consumer audiences.

- Experience creating developer-facing content, social-first creative, technical tutorials, or open-source projects is a plus.

What We Offer:

The expected contract pay range: $74-109 per hour. Contract compensation is determined by location, experience, and skillset. We have three regional pay ranges that are adjusted for cost of living (US1 +15%, US2 +7.5%, US3 Base), *learn more about our pay philosophy and cost of living adjustments.

Benefits may be available in accordance with applicable law and company policy, including eligibility based on hours worked and duration of assignment. 

Compensation

Additional Information

title: Senior Mobile Engineer
description:
Mattermost is the leading collaborative workflow platform for defense, intelligence, security, and critical infrastructure. Trusted by the U.S. Department of War and Fortune 500s, our platform runs on-premises and in private clouds, delivering secure messaging, file sharing, workflow automation, audio/screenshare, and project management—all with full data and operational control. Mattermost powers high-stakes workflows across mission planning, real-time, real-world operations, DevSecOps, incident response, and cyber defense—enabling secure collaboration from tactical edge and DDIL environments to enterprise HQ. Teams operate across web, desktop, and mobile, with embedded interoperability for Microsoft Teams, Outlook, and Microsoft 365.

To learn more, visit www.mattermost.com 

We are seeking a Senior Mobile Engineer to take ownership of the Mattermost mobile experience for teams working in defense, intelligence, and critical infrastructure. Our users operate in DDIL environments where connectivity may be disconnected, denied, intermittent, or limited, security is non-negotiable, and the software they depend on has to keep working.

Our mobile app is primarily React Native and TypeScript today, with native iOS and Android integrations. Your immediate focus will be making that experience more reliable and performant. Over time, you'll also help shape the next generation of our cross-platform mobile architecture.

You'll work hands-on across application and native layers, partner closely with platform and feature teams, work directly with customer-facing teams on field reports from constrained environments, and help raise the bar for how we observe, diagnose, and build mobile software.

Responsibilities

Reliability and Performance 

- Architect the app for DDIL and other constrained network environments

- Improve data and functional reliability across connection lifecycle, synchronization, recovery, and failure scenarios

- Own crash-free and release-health outcomes, using telemetry to proactively identify regressions and drive them through diagnosis to resolution

- Profile and improve performance across startup, networking, storage, rendering, memory, and battery usage

Mobile Platform Ownership 

- Own critical iOS and Android integrations and the boundaries between native and cross-platform code

- Maintain and evolve platform capabilities including push notifications, background execution, secure storage, app lifecycle, and real-time communications

- Build within mobile distribution and device-management constraints, including App Store, enterprise and MDM deployment, AppConfig, and Intune MAM

- Diagnose production issues from native traces, telemetry, device profiling, and sparse field logs

- Make architecture recommendations that balance near-term delivery with the long-term direction of the mobile platform

Craft and Delivery 

- Mentor engineers on mobile architecture, reliability, performance, and platform best practices

- Uphold security and compliance standards required by government and enterprise customers

- Contribute to the open-source codebase

- Use AI coding tools effectively, applying strong engineering judgment to increase output without compromising reliability or quality

What We Are Looking For

We care about what you've built and the problems you've solved — not how long you've been building. If you have strong outcomes to speak to in mobile engineering, we want to hear from you.

Required: 

- Deep expertise in iOS or Android development, with strong working knowledge of the other platform

- Strong understanding of mobile architecture, platform SDKs, lifecycle constraints, and networking fundamentals

- Experience building reliable mobile systems that behave predictably through unreliable connectivity, local state changes, synchronization, and recovery

- Strong mobile performance profiling and production debugging skills on real devices

- Experience using production data, crash metrics, and release-health signals to drive reliability improvements

- Experience making architecture recommendations and owning technical outcomes

- Ability and willingness to work across native and cross-platform codebases

- AI fluency and experience using coding agents to increase engineering output while applying judgment to ensure reliable outcomes

Preferred: 

- Experience with React Native and TypeScript

- Experience with mobile persistence, synchronization, or offline-capable systems

- Experience with real-time communications or platform media frameworks such as WebRTC, CallKit, or Android audio APIs

- Experience with enterprise mobile distribution, MDM, AppConfig, or Intune MAM

- Experience building mobile software for security-sensitive, regulated, or operationally constrained environments

- Open-source contributions

Why Mattermost

- Mission-driven work: Your contributions directly support the organizations and missions that depend on secure, reliable collaboration including the U.S. Department of War and critical infrastructure operators worldwide

- Remote-first culture: Work from anywhere with a globally distributed, high-trust team built for autonomy and ownership

- AI-forward environment: We actively adopt and build AI-enabled workflows. Agentic development is core craft here, not a novelty

- End-to-end ownership: Ship and own complex software across the full stack with real accountability for what you build

- Open source at the core: Be part of a vibrant developer community shaping the future of secure collaboration

Compensation

Mattermost takes a market-based approach to pay. Actual compensation may vary based on location, skills, experience, qualifications, and market conditions.

Target Salary Range: $165,000 – $215,000

U.S. Eligibility & Compliance

This role may require obtaining and maintaining a U.S. government security clearance. Candidates must meet federal eligibility requirements to be considered.

Applicants must meet eligibility requirements for access to export-controlled information as defined by U.S. export control laws, including EAR and ITAR. For more information visit the Bureau of Industry and Security and the Directorate of Defense Trade Controls .

Mattermost is an EEO Employer, we are a remote-first, open-source company.

We are continually working to expand our hiring in more countries and regions, ensuring compliance with local laws and regulations, which takes time.

Mattermost values your unique perspective—we welcome all applicants. We encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply and are committed to assessing candidates based on their skills and qualifications. We do not tolerate discrimination against staff or applicants based on race, religion, national origin, age, disability, pregnancy status, veteran status, or other personal characteristics.

If you require accommodations during the interview process, please let us know—we’re happy to assist.

title: Staff Software Engineer - Data
description:
About Dune 

Dune is on a mission to make crypto data accessible. We’re a collaborative multi-chain analytics platform used by thousands of developers, analysts, & investors to understand the on-chain world and the frontiers of finance. We’re a team of ~60 employees, working together across Europe and eastern US timezones 🌍️. We believe in our mission, and in building a powerful, open product that allows individuals and communities to do deep research into important ecosystems like Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, and many more. 

We’re backed by some of the world's best investors. In February 2022, we announced our Series B funding round led by Coatue and Union Square Ventures, an important milestone that allowed us to double down on our mission. We’re using the funds to educate, reward and empower a new generation of onchain analysts aka Wizards 🧙‍♀️

If you want to have one of the highest impact jobs on the planet, come join our wonderful team of Galaxy brains.

Learn more about us: 

Dune's Vision 

Values and working at Dune 

About the role 

Data Foundation owns how blockchain data enters Dune, how it is represented and how it’s delivered externally. This is a role that involves thinking about large distributed data systems, recognising traditional scaling patterns and software lifecycle pitfalls, and is ideal for anyone passionate about those topics.

You will be the engineer we hand ambiguous product requirements to, and will be comfortable coming back with a design, a sequence, and a set of tasks the team can pick up as well as building the hardest parts yourself.

In this role you will 

- 
Turn product requirements into technical requirements: model the domain, define the interfaces and the workflows, and navigate trade-offs

- 
Break large problems into work other engineers can own, and sequence it so we ship something useful early

- 
Drive high-impact architectural decisions across the data platform, and own components end to end from design through production

- 
Work across our stack, mainly Go, Kotlin, Rust and Python where they fit, choosing the right tool rather than the familiar one

- 
Design for correctness and performance under real volume: large-scale ingestion, distributed processing, and data lake storage

- 
Raise the bar on design reviews, testing, and how the team breaks work down

- 
Mentor engineers by example, in a fully distributed team

You might be a great fit if 

- 
You are a strong generalist with real computer science fundamentals, and you use them to adapt quickly to new technologies and problem spaces

- 
You reason from first principles: you make assumptions explicit, identify the constraints and invariants that matter, and derive the solution rather than reaching for a familiar pattern.

- 
You use computer science fundamentals as practical tools. You have designed and shipped distributed data systems, making their contracts, state transitions, invariants, and failure modes explicit. You know their fault models and scaling weaknesses

- 
You are comfortable with ambiguity : you will talk to product, to customers, and to the team, then commit to a scope and defend it

- 
You use AI tools well enough that they have changed how you work, you understand their failure modes and dislike ai-slop.

- 
You communicate clearly in writing and get the best out of a distributed team

Not required, but a plus 

- 
Experience with data lakes and formats such as Parquet, Iceberg or Deltalog

- 
Experience at a company where the data is the product

Perks & Benefits 

- 
A competitive salary and equity package 🚀. Both salary and equity is top 25% of companies in the space

- 
Our employee equity scheme has world-class employee-friendly terms with a heavily discounted strike price (~90%) and a 10-year exercise window

- 
5 weeks PTO + local public holidays (that can be swapped to suit you) 🏖

- 
A fully remote-first approach 🧑‍💻 within a distributed team with flexible working hours; you structure your own day 

- 
Say goodbye to meeting overload! We believe in a healthy mix of async and sync work, so you can focus on what truly matters—no more wasted time on endless meetings!

- 
Good health is important, so we offer private medical insurance, dental & vision as standard 🩺

- 
We believe in paid parental leave 👶 to help you celebrate this important milestone, transition to your new life, and bond with your new baby. We offer 16 weeks to primary and 6 weeks to secondary caregivers, fully paid. Plus a 2-week part-time phased return at full pay to help you get used to your new (and slightly more complex!) schedule

- 
Quarterly offsites in various exciting locations as a company or team to connect, work together and have fun (so far in Tuscany 🇮🇹 Berlin 🇩🇪 Austria 🇦🇹 and Athens 🇬🇷).

- 
On top of this 👆each person gets a yearly travel allowance to connect and co-work with someone or a team of people for a few days.

- 
An allowance for your at-home setup, to ensure you are happy, comfortable and productive. If you prefer a local co-working space, we’ll pay for your desk.

- 
Work with some of the best people you’ll ever get to meet!

- 
And of course, you get some awesome Dune swag ! ✌️😎

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

title: Senior Software Engineer (.NET) (f/m/d)
Software Engineering Manager (Backend SaaS)
description:
Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.

The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing.

We are hiring an engineering manager to lead the reboot of our Landscape systems management solution for Ubuntu.

Ubuntu is growing rapidly in the enterprise, with estates expanding from cloud, to bare metal servers, to vSphere clusters, and of course desktops and devices. Ubuntu is easy to deploy and configure, one node at a time, but it's difficult to know where you stand on policy and compliance, patch management, or access control across a large estate. Ubuntu used to be under the radar in the enterprise, but it is now becoming an official platform for many companies. Those enterprises very much want a high quality way to manage their Ubuntu estate.

We started work on Landscape many years ago, and the current generation of the service reflects the choices of the day. We now have the opportunity to invest significantly in a team to bring a fresh new vision for large-scale Ubuntu estate management to the project. That doesn't make this a greenfield opportunity - we have a system that serves thousands of deployments - but we know we want to step back and give it a big new push, letting go of some things that are no longer so important, and embracing a range of new priorities. This role is the critical engineering leadership role for that mission.

Today we use Python, PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, HAProxy, and have a ReactJS front end. In other web services projects we use more Golang these days. Our next wave of Landscape engineering is an opportunity to raise the bar on SAAS and on-prem solution technologies, architectures, patterns and operations. Our goal is to make it easy for enterprises to own a few Landscape instances that serve their global estate, and to be able to apply policy and know intuitively where they stand - globally - in a very complex world of mixed Ubuntu versions, substrates and flavours.

Engineering managers at Canonical bring both technical and management skills to the leadership of their teams. You will work closely with product managers, and produce an engineering roadmap with ambitious and achievable goals. A successful applicant will be capable of growing a team of engineers, collaborating with other engineering and business teams at Canonical, and providing periodic updates about successes and areas of improvement.

As an engineering manager at Canonical you must be technically strong, but your responsibility is to run an effective team and develop the colleagues you manage. You are expected to help them grow as engineers, do important work, do it outstandingly well, find professional and personal satisfaction, and work well with colleagues and community. Technical leadership experience and a background in software engineering are necessary prerequisites for this role. You will be expected to lead, challenge, and develop strong engineers, positively influence the culture, facilitate technical delivery, and work with your team on strategy and execution.

We work in Python and Golang, and expect engineering managers to be fluent in the language, architecture and components that their team uses. Code reviews and architectural leadership are part of the job. As manager, the commitment to healthy engineering practices, documentation, quality and performance optimisation are equally important technical responsibilities, as is the requirement for fair and clear management, and the obligation to ensure a high performing team.

Key responsibilities

- Build and lead a team of engineers in your region

- Develop talent through coaching, mentoring, feedback, and hands-on career development

- Demonstrate sound engineering principles and directly contribute toward your team's goals

- Set and manage expectations with other engineering teams, management, and external stakeholders

- Lead modern, agile software development practices

- Ensure a healthy, collaborative engineering culture in line with the company values

- Be an active part of the leadership team and collaborate with other leaders in the organisation

- Build automated, highly reliable image delivery, testing and publication pipelines

- Engage with many other teams at Canonical, as well as the open source community and commercial partners

- Work from home with global travel 4-6 weeks per year for internal and external events

Valued skills and experience

- You love to mentor, develop and grow people, and have a track record of doing it

- You are knowledgeable and passionate about software development

- You are focused on success and the delivery of timely, high quality software

- You have experience and commitment to agile development methodologies

- You have a Bachelor’s or equivalent in Computer Science, STEM or similar degree

- Software development experience in Python or Golang

- Effective written and verbal communication skills

- Practical experience with Linux system administration

What we offer colleagues

We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognize outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.

- Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person

- Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year

- Annual compensation review

- Recognition rewards

- Annual holiday leave

- Maternity and paternity leave

- Team Member Assistance Program & Wellness Platform

- Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues

- Priority Pass and travel upgrades for long-haul company events

About Canonical

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open-source projects and the platform for AI, IoT, and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence; in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Most colleagues at Canonical have worked from home since our inception in 2004.​ Working here is a step into the future and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.

Canonical is an equal opportunity employer 

We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.
